fields.name: The Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three: which standard classes $b_j$ survive the mod-3 Adams spectral sequence
fields.field: Stable homotopy theory; odd-primary Kervaire invariant
fields.statement: In the mod-$p$ Adams spectral sequence $\mathrm{Ext}_{\mathcal A_p}^{s,t}(\mathbb F_p,\mathbb F_p)\Rightarrow \pi_*^S$, the odd-primary analogues of the Kervaire classes are $b_j\in E_2^{2,2(p-1)p^{j+1}}$. Toda showed that $b_1$ supports a differential at every odd prime, and Ravenel (1978) proved that no $b_j$ with $j\ge1$ survives for $p\ge5$. At $p=3$ the argument fails: $b_0$ (stem 10) and $b_2$ (stem 106) survive, and the fate of the higher classes was open; Hill, Hopkins and Ravenel proposed attacking it through the action of $C_9$ on height-six Morava $E$-theory. The strong form also asks for representatives of order $p$. At $p=3$, for which $j$ does $b_j$ survive to $E_\infty$, and when it does, is it detected by an element of order three?
fields.posedBy: Douglas Ravenel (1978), whose odd-primary nonexistence theorem left p = 3 open; program of Hill, Hopkins and Ravenel (2011)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Ravenel, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1978) for the p >= 5 theorem and the special behaviour at three, Hill-Hopkins-Ravenel's 2011 manuscript on the 3-primary problem, and Belmont-Ray's 'Towards the p=3 Kervaire invariant problem'. The order-p refinement is Selick's (1983) reformulation.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. Single manuscript dated September 24, 2026. The paper says it uses classical inputs (Toda's differentials, the Miller-Ravenel-Wilson two-line, Amelotte's and Selick's criteria) and proves Belmont-Ray's coefficient model itself.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the abstract, introduction, Theorem 1.1 and the reduction of the proof to its two branches were read against the problem as Ravenel and Hill-Hopkins-Ravenel framed it; the proof was not refereed. No Lean formalization exists for this family. The paper states its scope: the standard family $b_j$ in the mod-3 Adams spectral sequence, not the classical prime-two Kervaire problem. The exclusion of $j\ge4$ runs through a height-six $C_9$ detector and finite-page outgoing differentials; the paper says it does not use the 972-periodicity or the degree $-2$ vanishing clause of Belmont-Ray's Conjecture 0.1, and it claims to refute the latter clause.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: at $p=3$, $K=K_3=\{0,2,3\}$, i.e. $b_j$ survives to $E_\infty$ exactly for $j=0,2,3$ (stems 10, 106 and 322), and each surviving class is detected by an element of additive order three; $b_1$ and all $b_j$ with $j\ge4$ die. The new content is the order-three element in stem 322 and the exclusion of every $j\ge4$. Corollaries via Amelotte and Selick: $\Omega S^{2n+1}\{3\}$ splits nontrivially exactly for $n\in\{3,27,81\}$, and the Anick space $T^{2n+1}(3)$ is homotopy associative exactly for those $n$. Side result: an infinite-order class in $\pi_{2n}(E_6^{hC_9})$ for every $n$, refuting the full-gap clause of Belmont-Ray's Conjecture 0.1. Not covered: other odd primes (already settled for $p\ge5$) or the prime-two problem.

fields.significanceNote: The last open prime of the odd-primary Kervaire invariant problem, open since Ravenel's 1978 theorem and the subject of a proposed Hill-Hopkins-Ravenel program; well known in stable homotopy theory but far less famous than the prime-two problem. Placed just above Smith-Toda complexes at every height (30), below the Curtis conjecture on the stable Hurewicz image (48) and the Kervaire conjecture for groups (55).

fields.name: Spontaneous magnetization of the three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet at low temperature (Lieb's Problem A)
fields.field: Quantum spin systems; phase transitions
fields.statement: The nearest-neighbour quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet on $\mathbb Z^d$ has Hamiltonian $H=-\sum_{|x-y|=1}\mathbf S_x\cdot\mathbf S_y$ with spin-$S$ matrices at each site. Mermin and Wagner excluded order at positive temperature for $d\le2$; Frohlich-Simon-Spencer proved ordering for the classical model in $d\ge3$ and Dyson-Lieb-Simon for quantum antiferromagnets, but the reflection-positivity method gives no infrared bound for the quantum ferromagnet. Lieb listed the problem in 1999 (Problem A), and it was still described as open in 2025. Does the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet in dimension $d\ge3$, for every spin $S$, order at sufficiently low positive temperature, i.e. have an equilibrium state with nonzero spontaneous magnetization at zero field?
fields.posedBy: Elliott H. Lieb (1999, Problem A of his list of statistical-mechanics problems); obstruction noted by Dyson, Lieb and Simon (1978)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Lieb (1999) Problem A as the explicit posing and Seiringer's 2025 account, which states it with a volume-averaged finite-volume two-point order parameter. Dyson-Lieb-Simon (1978, pp. 339-340) already explained why their method did not reach the ferromagnet.

fields.name: Bloch's $T^{3/2}$ law for the three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet
fields.field: Quantum spin systems; spin-wave theory
fields.statement: Bloch's spin-wave theory (1930) predicts that the spontaneous magnetization of a three-dimensional ferromagnet falls below saturation by an amount proportional to $T^{3/2}$, with a coefficient fixed by the quadratic one-magnon dispersion; for the nearest-neighbour spin-$S$ Heisenberg model the deficit is $\zeta(3/2)(8\pi^{3/2}S^{3/2})^{-1}T^{3/2}$ to leading order. Dyson (1956) analysed spin-wave interactions and the higher-order terms, but not as a rigorous fixed-spin proof, and Correggi-Giuliani-Seiringer (2015) proved the corresponding free-energy asymptotics, which do not control the zero-field derivative. Is it true, for the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet on $\mathbb Z^3$ at fixed spin, that $S-m(\beta)\sim c\,\beta^{-3/2}$ as $\beta\to\infty$ with Bloch's coefficient, where $m$ is the spontaneous magnetization?
fields.posedBy: Felix Bloch (1930), spin-wave prediction; developed by Holstein-Primakoff (1940) and Dyson (1956)
fields.ageNote: A physical prediction stated precisely in print. The manuscript cites Bloch (1930) and Dyson (1956), notes that Dyson's higher-order estimates were not a rigorous proof, and cites Lieb (1999) and Seiringer (2025) for the ordering problem underneath it.

fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every fixed spin $S$ and every nonnegative symmetric finite-range coupling $J$ on $\mathbb Z^3$ whose support generates $\mathbb Z^3$, $\lim_{\beta\to\infty}\beta^{3/2}(S-m_{S,J}(\beta))=\zeta(3/2)/(8\pi^{3/2}\sqrt{\det D_{S,J}})$, with $D_{S,J}=\frac S2\sum_z J(z)zz^{\mathsf T}$; nearest-neighbour gives $\zeta(3/2)/(8\pi^{3/2}S^{3/2})$. Companions: the first lattice correction $3\zeta(5/2)(\beta S)^{-5/2}/(128\pi^{3/2})$ for nearest-neighbour couplings, deficit equal to the ideal-magnon density up to $o(\beta^{-5/2})$; and a spherical magnetization law for the symmetric zero-field magnetization on periodic cubes. Not shown: Dyson's $T^4$ interaction term, dimensions other than three, or uniformity in $S$.

fields.name: Yau's dimension comparison for harmonic functions of integer polynomial growth under nonnegative Ricci curvature
fields.field: Riemannian geometry; harmonic functions of polynomial growth
fields.statement: For a complete Riemannian manifold $(M^n,g)$ let $\mathcal H_d(M)$ be the space of harmonic functions with $|u(x)|\le C(1+d(o,x))^d$ and $h_d(M)=\dim\mathcal H_d(M)$. On $\mathbb R^n$, $h_k=\binom{n+k-1}{k}+\binom{n+k-2}{k-1}$ for integer $k\ge1$. Li and Tam proved $h_1(M)\le n+1$ when $\mathrm{Ric}\ge0$, Colding and Minicozzi proved finite dimensionality and bounds of optimal order $k^{n-1}$, and Donnelly found counterexamples at non-integer degrees between one and two. Yau asked about sharp Euclidean comparison. Does $\mathrm{Ric}_g\ge0$ imply $h_k(M^n)\le h_k(\mathbb R^n)$ for every integer $k\ge1$?
fields.posedBy: Shing-Tung Yau, Open problems in geometry, Problem 48
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Yau's problem list in Schoen-Yau, Lectures on Differential Geometry (International Press, 1994), Problem 48. Whether an earlier list states the integer-degree comparison was not checked.

The principal manuscript ships an optional exact integer check of its finite spectral selection for n = 16, k = 50000, which it says does not verify the metric.

That states the headline negative answer. The challenge file states MainClaim through a placeholder axiom; the solution module proves main as a theorem, and the comparator's permitted axioms exclude custom ones. Not rebuilt here. The 3D companion is not formalized.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are an even $n\ge8$ (the paper allows $n=16$), an integer $k\ge2$ ($k=50000$) and a complete smooth metric on $\mathbb R^n$ with $\mathrm{Ric}\ge0$, Euclidean near the origin, asymptotic volume ratio strictly between 0 and 1, and $h_k>h_k(\mathbb R^n)$; the metric has nonunique tangent cones at infinity. fields.name: The sharp constant for the terminal leave of random triangle removal (triangle case of the Joos-Kühn conjecture)
fields.field: Random graph processes; random greedy packing
fields.statement: Start from $K_n$ and repeatedly delete the three edges of a uniformly random remaining triangle until none is left; let $F_n$ be the number of edges remaining. Bollobas and Erdos conjectured (1990) that $F_n$ has order $n^{3/2}$; after work of Spencer, Rodl-Thoma and Grable, Bohman, Frieze and Lubetzky proved $F_n=n^{3/2+o(1)}$ with high probability (2015). Joos and Kuhn (2024) studied removal of a general strictly balanced hypergraph and conjectured (Conjecture 16.2) an asymptotic constant for the terminal leave, whose triangle case predicts $F_n/n^{3/2}\to 1/(2\sqrt2)$ in probability. Is that so?
fields.posedBy: Felix Joos and Marcus Kühn (Conjecture 16.2 of The hypergraph removal process); order of magnitude conjectured by Bollobás and Erdős (1990)
fields.ageNote: arXiv 2412.15039, first version 19 December 2024; the manuscript cites the conjecture's numbering from version 2. The Bollobas-Erdos order-of-magnitude conjecture is cited through Bohman-Frieze-Lubetzky (2015).

The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. Single manuscript dated September 25, 2026. It states that its only external proof input is Joos and Kuhn's early-prefix control; all continuation estimates are proved in the paper.

That is the headline. Not rebuilt here. Entry is partial because the conjecture covers general strictly balanced hypergraphs.

fields.name: Erdős Problem 304: are all fractions $a/b$ sums of $O(\log\log b)$ distinct unit fractions?
fields.field: Egyptian fractions; additive combinatorics
fields.statement: For integers $1\le a<b$ let $N(a,b)$ be the least $k$ such that $a/b=1/n_1+\cdots+1/n_k$ with integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$, and let $N(b)=\max_{1\le a<b}N(a,b)$. Erdos (1950) proved $\log\log b\ll N(b)\ll\log b/\log\log b$, and Vose (1985) improved the upper bound to $N(b)\ll\sqrt{\log b}$. Is it true that $N(b)\ll\log\log b$?

fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are absolute $c_1,c_2>0$ and $b_0$ with $c_1\log\log b\le N(b)\le c_2\log\log b$ for $b\ge b_0$; the upper bound holds for every numerator. Corollaries: the number $F(k)$ of $k$-term expansions of 1 satisfies $\log\log F(k)\asymp k$ (Erdős-Graham asked for estimates), and the least integer $v(k)\ge2$ missing from all $k$-term expansions of 1 satisfies $e^{e^{k/600}}\le v(k)\le 1+k^{2^{k-1}}$ eventually, so $\log\log v(k)\asymp k$, answering the growth question of Erdős Problem 293 up to constants. Not shown: the optimal constants, or control of denominator sizes (unlike Tenenbaum-Yokota).

fields.name: The Lazić-Peternell Generalised Abundance Conjecture for projective klt pairs
fields.field: Birational geometry; minimal model program
fields.statement: Let $(X,B)$ be a projective klt pair with $K_X+B$ pseudo-effective, and let $L$ be a nef Cartier divisor such that $K_X+B+L$ is nef. Lazic and Peternell conjectured that $K_X+B+L$ is numerically equivalent to a semiample $\mathbb Q$-divisor (numerical equivalence is needed: a nontorsion degree-zero line bundle on an elliptic curve is nef with no sections). They proved it for surfaces and for threefolds where $K_X+B$ has positive numerical dimension, and reduced it in general to the minimal model program, abundance and a semiampleness conjecture on Calabi-Yau pairs. Is $K_X+B+L$ always numerically equivalent to a semiample divisor?
fields.posedBy: Vladimir Lazić and Thomas Peternell (On Generalised Abundance, I)
fields.ageNote: arXiv 1808.00438 (2018), published Publ. RIMS 56 (2020); the manuscript cites the arXiv v2 numbering.

fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for a projective klt $\mathbb Q$-pair $(X,B)$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero with $K_X+B$ pseudo-effective and $M$ nef $\mathbb Q$-Cartier on $X$, if $K_X+B+M$ is nef then it is numerically equivalent to a semiample $\mathbb Q$-Cartier divisor. Corollary: on a klt pair with $K_X+B\equiv0$ every nef $\mathbb Q$-Cartier divisor is numerically semiample. New ingredient: a nef divisor of full nef dimension on a klt Calabi-Yau pair is big. Kahler companion: for smooth compact Kahler $X$, snc $B$ with coefficients below one and nef $M$, $c_1(K_X+B+M)$ is represented in Bott-Chern cohomology by a semiample line bundle. Not shown: semiampleness of $K_X+B+M$ itself, lc pairs, or nef data living only on a higher model.

fields.name: Existence of minimal models and Mori fibre spaces for projective log canonical pairs, in generalized-pair form
fields.shortName: Minimal model existence for lc pairs
fields.field: Birational geometry; minimal model program
fields.statement: The minimal model conjecture in its existence form asserts that every projective log canonical pair $(X,B)$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero has a minimal model (a birational model with nef $K_Y+B_Y$ and no worse discrepancies) when $K_X+B$ is pseudo-effective, and a Mori fibre space otherwise. Birkar-Cascini-Hacon-McKernan proved this for klt pairs with big boundary or big adjoint; the general case was open in dimension at least five, and for generalized pairs (Birkar-Zhang) carrying a fixed nef part. Does every projective (generalized) log canonical $\mathbb Q$-pair admit a minimal model or a Mori fibre space?

fields.name: Must a closed manifold admitting a metric without conjugate points admit a metric of nonpositive curvature?
fields.shortName: No conjugate points vs nonpositive curvature
fields.field: Riemannian geometry; manifolds without conjugate points
fields.statement: A Riemannian metric has no conjugate points if no nonzero Jacobi field along a geodesic vanishes twice. Nonpositive sectional curvature implies this, and Gulliver showed that individual metrics without conjugate points may have positive curvature somewhere, but his examples live on manifolds that already carry negatively curved metrics. On surfaces the answer is yes by uniformization. Ivanov and Kapovitch asked, and Burns and Matveev repeated for dimension three, whether every closed manifold that admits a metric without conjugate points also admits a metric of nonpositive sectional curvature. Is that true?

fields.name: Erdős Problem 416: does $V(2x)/V(x)\to2$ for the number $V(x)$ of totient values up to $x$, and is there an asymptotic formula?
fields.field: Multiplicative number theory; values of arithmetic functions
fields.statement: Let $V(x)$ count the integers $v\le x$ for which $\varphi(m)=v$ is solvable. fields.name: Letrouit's square-root stability conjecture for Brenier maps from a uniform convex source
fields.field: Optimal transport; quantitative stability
fields.statement: Let $\rho$ be the uniform probability measure on a compact convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, and for a probability measure $\mu$ on a fixed compact set $Y$ let $T_\mu$ be the quadratic optimal (Brenier) map pushing $\rho$ to $\mu$. fields.name: The Barendregt-Geuvers-Klop conjecture for beta reduction: weak normalization implies strong normalization in every pure type system
fields.field: Type theory; lambda calculus; pure type systems
fields.statement: A pure type system is given by a set of sorts $\mathcal S$, axioms $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal S^2$ and product rules $\mathcal R\subseteq\mathcal S^3$, with full $\beta$-reduction allowed everywhere, including inside type annotations. The system is weakly normalizing if every legal expression in every valid context has a $\beta$-normal form, and strongly normalizing if no such expression admits an infinite $\beta$-reduction sequence. Strong normalization was known to follow from weak normalization only for restricted classes (Sorensen; Barthe, Hatcliff and Sorensen for nondependent systems). Is every weakly $\beta$-normalizing pure type system strongly $\beta$-normalizing?
fields.posedBy: Barendregt, Geuvers and Klop; stated by Herman Geuvers as Conjecture 8.1.2 of his thesis (Nijmegen, 1993)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Geuvers's 1993 thesis (Conjecture 8.1.2) for the system-wide conjecture, which he states for both beta and beta-eta reduction. The name credits Barendregt, Geuvers and Klop; the thesis is the earliest written statement the manuscript gives.

fields.name: Wu's bounded-domain question for negatively pinched Kahler manifolds: is a complete simply connected Kahler manifold with pinched negative curvature biholomorphic to a bounded domain?
fields.field: Kahler geometry; several complex variables
fields.statement: In complex dimension one, a complete simply connected surface with curvature bounded above by a negative constant is biholomorphic to the disc. H. Wu (1967) asked whether a complete simply connected Kahler manifold with nonpositive sectional curvature and holomorphic sectional curvature bounded above by a negative constant must be biholomorphic to a bounded domain. Wu and Yau (2019, Conjecture 4.3) state the two-sided version: if a simply connected complete Kahler manifold $M$ of complex dimension $n$ has every real sectional curvature between two negative constants, $-B\le K\le -A<0$, must $M$ be biholomorphic to a bounded (pseudoconvex) domain in $\mathbb C^n$?

fields.name: The PCP-for-PPAD conjecture of Babichenko, Papadimitriou and Rubinstein (quasilinear form)
fields.field: Computational complexity; PPAD and equilibrium computation
fields.statement: End-of-Line is the canonical PPAD-complete problem: given successor and predecessor circuits on $\{0,1\}^n$ with a known source, find another endpoint. A generalized circuit asks for an assignment of values in $[0,1]$ to wires that $\varepsilon$-satisfies local arithmetic, comparison and Boolean gates. Rubinstein proved PPAD-hardness for constant $\varepsilon$ when every gate must be satisfied. Babichenko, Papadimitriou and Rubinstein (2016) conjectured a PCP analogue: are there constants $\varepsilon,\delta>0$ and a quasilinear-size reduction from End-of-Line to generalized circuits such that any assignment $\varepsilon$-satisfying all but a $\delta$ fraction of gates, wherever the failures lie, yields an End-of-Line solution in polynomial time?

This also implies the weaker polynomial-size PCP-for-PPAD statement. It does not by itself give new Nash lower bounds; those (Rubinstein, Golowich) still need an exponential-time hypothesis for PPAD.

fields.name: The elastic Calderon problem in three dimensions: do boundary measurements determine smooth isotropic Lame moduli?
fields.field: Inverse problems; linear elasticity
fields.statement: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded connected smooth domain and $\lambda,\mu\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega)$ Lame moduli with $\mu>0$, $3\lambda+2\mu>0$. The static displacement-to-traction map $\Lambda_{\lambda,\mu}$ sends boundary displacements $f$ to the tractions $\sigma_{\lambda,\mu}(u_f)n$ of the solution of $\operatorname{div}(\lambda(\operatorname{div}u)I+2\mu e(u))=0$ with trace $f$. Nakamura and Uhlmann claimed global uniqueness in 1994; their 2003 erratum proved it only when $\|\nabla\mu_j\|_{C^m}$ is small. Does $\Lambda_{\lambda_1,\mu_1}=\Lambda_{\lambda_2,\mu_2}$ imply $\lambda_1=\lambda_2$ and $\mu_1=\mu_2$ for all such smooth moduli?

fields.statement: Fix a prime $p$ and height $n\ge1$, and let $L_{K(n)}S$ be the Bousfield localization of the $p$-complete sphere at Morava $K$-theory $K(n)$. It is not connective, so finiteness must be controlled degree by degree. At height one the answer follows from the classical computation; at height two and $p\ge5$ Hovey and Strickland derived it from Shimomura's computations. Is $\pi_t L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge$ a finitely generated $\mathbb Z_p$-module for every prime $p$, every height $n$ and every integer $t$?

Combined with the rational computation of Barthel-Schlank-Stapleton-Weinstein this fixes the free ranks. The key step is finiteness of continuous cohomology of the stabilizer with mod $p$ Lubin-Tate coefficients. It gives no bound on the number of generators or the torsion as $p$, $n$, $t$ vary, computes no torsion, and does not extend to all invertible $K(n)$-local spectra (known to fail at height two).

fields.name: Log abundance for threefolds in characteristic $p>3$ in numerical dimension one
fields.shortName: Char p threefold log abundance, nu = 1
fields.field: Birational geometry in positive characteristic; minimal model program
fields.statement: The abundance conjecture predicts that if $(X,B)$ is a projective log canonical pair and $K_X+B$ is nef, then $K_X+B$ is semiample. For threefolds over $\mathbb C$ this is a theorem (Miyaoka, Kawamata, Keel-Matsuki-McKernan). Over algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p>0$ it remains open; Zheng Xu proved nonvanishing for $p>3$, abundance in nef dimension at most two, and abundance in numerical dimension two. Is abundance true for projective log canonical threefold pairs in characteristic $p>3$, in particular when $K_X+B$ is nef of numerical dimension one?

fields.name: The Monge (co-motion) ansatz for three-marginal Coulomb transport in $\mathbb R^3$: is the optimum always attained by maps?
fields.field: Multi-marginal optimal transport; density functional theory
fields.statement: For a probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^3$, minimize $\int c\,d\pi$ over couplings $\pi$ with three marginals equal to $\mu$, where $c(x_1,x_2,x_3)=\sum_{i<j}|x_i-x_j|^{-1}$. In the strictly correlated electron limit of density functional theory one expects optimizers of co-motion (Monge) form $(\mathrm{Id},T_2,T_3)_\#\mu$ with measure-preserving maps. This holds for two marginals (Cotar-Friesecke-Kluppelberg) and in one dimension (Colombo-De Pascale-Di Marino). If $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with finite Coulomb transport value, is the minimum always attained by a Monge plan?
fields.posedBy: Recorded by G. Friesecke, A. Gerolin and P. Gori-Giorgi (2022 preprint of their DFT chapter, Theorem 2.4 and discussion); still stated open by Friesecke (January 2026)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites the 2022 preprint of Friesecke-Gerolin-Gori-Giorgi as recording the higher-dimensional question and Friesecke (January 2026) for the three-particle Coulomb case in R^3 being open. The co-motion ansatz itself goes back to Seidl, Gori-Giorgi and Savin (2007) and earlier SCE work.

fields.name: Gigli's conjecture: Alexandrov curvature bounds are characterized by his distributional sectional curvature on noncollapsed RCD spaces
fields.field: Metric geometry; RCD spaces and Alexandrov spaces
fields.statement: On an $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ metric measure space, Gigli (2019) defined a distributional Riemann curvature tensor $R(X,Y,Z,W)$ acting on test vector fields and test functions. Let $n\ge2$, $\kappa\in\mathbb R$ and $(M,d)$ complete and separable. Gigli conjectured that $(M,d)$ is an $n$-dimensional Alexandrov space of curvature at least $\kappa$ if and only if $(M,d,\mathcal H^n)$ has full support, is $\mathrm{RCD}((n-1)\kappa,n)$, and satisfies $R(X,Y,Y,X)(f)\ge\kappa\int f(|X|^2|Y|^2-\langle X,Y\rangle^2)\,d\mathcal H^n$ for all test fields $X,Y$ and nonnegative test functions $f$. Is this characterization true?
fields.posedBy: Nicola Gigli, Conjecture 1.1 of 'Riemann curvature tensor on RCD spaces and possible applications' (2019)

fields.name: Kalton's question: does the Lipschitz-free space of every uniformly discrete metric space have the bounded approximation property?
fields.shortName: Kalton's BAP question for uniformly discrete free spaces
fields.field: Banach space theory; Lipschitz-free spaces
fields.statement: For a pointed metric space $(M,d,o)$, the Lipschitz-free space $\mathcal F(M)$ is the closed span of the evaluations $\delta_x$ in $\mathrm{Lip}_0(M)^*$. Kalton showed that if $M$ is uniformly discrete ($d(x,y)\ge\theta>0$ for $x\ne y$) then $\mathcal F(M)$ has the approximation property, and Dalet proved the metric approximation property for countable proper spaces. Kalton asked, and Godefroy-Ozawa (Question 1) and Godefroy's survey (Problem 6.2) restated: if $M$ is uniformly discrete, must $\mathcal F(M)$ have the bounded approximation property, that is, can the finite-rank approximants of the identity be chosen with a uniform norm bound?
fields.posedBy: Nigel Kalton (Collectanea Mathematica 2004, remarks after Proposition 4.4); restated by Godefroy and Ozawa (2014, Question 1) and Godefroy (2015 survey, Problem 6.2)

The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author.

That is the headline claim. Not rebuilt here. A separate challenge, RealL1Renorming, covers the quantitative renorming of $\ell_1$.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a countable, unbounded, nonproper pointed metric space with $d(x,y)\ge1$ for distinct points whose real Lipschitz-free space has AP but fails $\lambda$-BAP for every finite $\lambda$. It is built as a wedge of bounded blocks (Theorem 1.2) in which a finite anchor set defeats every finite-rank operator of norm at most $p$. Real scalars only; the proper countable case is excluded by Dalet's theorem.

fields.name: The Hovey-Strickland conjecture: the thick tensor ideals of dualizable K(n)-local spectra
fields.field: Chromatic homotopy theory; tensor-triangular geometry
fields.statement: Fix a prime $p$ and a height $n\ge1$, and let $\mathcal D_{(n,p)}$ be the homotopy category of dualizable $K(n)$-local spectra, with tensor product $L_{K(n)}(X\wedge Y)$. A thick tensor ideal is a full subcategory closed under retracts, cofiber sequences, suspensions and tensoring with every object. For $0\le k\le n$ the localization of a finite type-$k$ spectrum generates a thick tensor ideal $\mathcal D_k$, giving a chain $\mathcal D_0\supsetneq\mathcal D_1\supsetneq\cdots\supsetneq\mathcal D_n\supsetneq0$. By analogy with the Hopkins-Smith thick subcategory theorem for finite spectra, Hovey and Strickland (1999) conjectured that this chain is everything. Barthel, Heard and Naumann proved it at height two and showed it follows from Chai's invariant-ideal conjecture. For every prime and every height, are the thick tensor ideals of $\mathcal D_{(n,p)}$ exactly the $n+2$ ideals $\mathcal D_0,\ldots,\mathcal D_n,0$, so that the Balmer spectrum is a chain of $n+1$ points?
fields.posedBy: Mark Hovey and Neil Strickland (Morava K-theories and localisation, Mem. AMS 1999, Section 12); restated by Barthel, Heard and Naumann (2022)

The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. fields.name: Chai's conjecture on stabilizer-invariant ideals of the Lubin-Tate deformation ring
fields.field: Arithmetic of formal groups; Lubin-Tate space
fields.statement: Let $\Gamma_n$ be the height-$n$ Honda formal group over $\overline{\mathbb F}_p$ and $E_0=W(\mathbb F_{p^n})[[u_1,\ldots,u_{n-1}]]$ its Lubin-Tate deformation ring, on which the Morava stabilizer group $A_n^\times$ acts by changing the marking. The height ideals $I_h=(p,u_1,\ldots,u_{h-1})$, $1\le h\le n$, cut out the loci where the deformed formal group has height at least $h$; with $0$ they are invariant primes. Chai (1996), studying the group action on the closed fiber of Lubin-Tate space, proposed that invariant irreducible formal loci should be height loci; Hovey and Strickland asked the same about invariant primes (Problem 16.8), and Barthel, Heard and Naumann made it precise as Chai's Hope for finite residue fields. For an open subgroup $U$ of the stabilizer, are $0,I_1,\ldots,I_n$ the only proper $U$-stable primes of $E_0$, and $0,I_1,\ldots,I_n,E_0$ the only $U$-invariant radical ideals?

fields.name: The Phillips-Toms conjecture for minimal homeomorphisms: radius of comparison equals half the mean dimension
fields.field: Operator algebras; C*-dynamics and mean dimension
fields.statement: For a minimal homeomorphism $h$ of an infinite compact metrizable space $X$, the crossed product $C(X)\rtimes_h\mathbb Z$ is a simple unital nuclear C*-algebra. Toms's radius of comparison $\mathrm{rc}(A)$ is the least $r$ such that $d_\tau(a)+r<d_\tau(b)$ for every trace $\tau$ forces Cuntz subequivalence $a\precsim b$; the Lindenstrauss-Weiss mean dimension $\mathrm{mdim}(X,h)$ measures dimension per orbit coordinate. Giol and Kerr built minimal systems of positive mean dimension with large radius of comparison; Phillips proved $\mathrm{rc}\le1+36\,\mathrm{mdim}$, Elliott and Niu settled zero mean dimension, and Niu proved $\mathrm{rc}\le\frac12\mathrm{mdim}$. The Phillips-Toms conjecture, recorded for integer actions by Elliott-Niu and as Problem XXXVI of Schafhauser-Tikuisis-White, predicts equality. Is $\mathrm{rc}(C(X)\rtimes_h\mathbb Z)=\frac12\mathrm{mdim}(X,h)$ for every such system, including the value $\infty$?
fields.posedBy: N. Christopher Phillips and Andrew Toms; integer-action form recorded by Elliott and Niu (Duke 2017) and as Problem XXXVI of Schafhauser-Tikuisis-White

fields.name: The Ford-Konyagin-Luca conjecture: the prime factors of $p-1$ follow the Poisson-Dirichlet law
fields.field: Analytic number theory; smooth shifted primes
fields.statement: For a prime $p$, list the prime factors of $p-1$ with multiplicity in decreasing order $q_1(p)\ge q_2(p)\ge\cdots$ and set $V_j(p)=\log q_j(p)/\log(p-1)$. For a uniformly random integer the analogous normalized factor sizes converge to the Poisson-Dirichlet law $\mathrm{PD}(1)$ (Billingsley, Donnelly-Grimmett). Ford, Konyagin and Luca (2010, Section 6, Conjecture 5) conjectured the same for shifted primes. The first coordinate already contains the shifted-prime Dickman law stated by Granville, $\#\{p\le x:P^+(p-1)\le x^{1/u}\}\sim\pi(x)\rho(u)$ for fixed $u$; unconditionally only lower bounds of size $x/(\log x)^C$ for $P^+(p-1)\le x^{0.2844}$ were known (Baker-Harman, Lichtman), and the full law was known under Elliott-Halberstam (Bharadwaj-Rodgers). With $p$ uniform among primes up to $x$, does $(V_1(p),V_2(p),\ldots)$ converge in finite-dimensional distributions to $\mathrm{PD}(1)$ as $x\to\infty$?
fields.posedBy: Kevin Ford, Sergei Konyagin and Florian Luca (Prime chains and Pratt trees, GAFA 2010, Section 6, Conjecture 5)
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results in the release were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with one fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This family is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The principal manuscript builds on graph and ideal-kernel estimates proved in the companion 'Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers' (same date, separate entry for Erdos Problem #821); a third companion (17 September) uses the same machinery for primes with mu(p-1) = 1.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 and the history section were read against Conjecture 5 of Ford-Konyagin-Luca as the manuscript quotes it (same multiplicity convention, normalization and equal weighting of primes). No Lean formalization exists for this family. The claim is unconditional and reaches what was previously known only under the Elliott-Halberstam conjecture; the manuscript says that unconditional distribution results (level one half) cover only part of the simplex and that its extraction argument reaches every compact subset with coordinate sum below one. A claim of this strength should be read as unverified until specialists examine it. It imports estimates from the companion manuscript. Not refereed here.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $k$ and bounded continuous $F$ on $[0,1]^k$, the average of $F(V_1(p),\ldots,V_k(p))$ over primes $3\le p\le x$ tends to $\mathbb E F(L_1,\ldots,L_k)$ with $(L_j)\sim\mathrm{PD}(1)$, unconditionally and with equal weight on each prime. The manuscript notes this gives Granville's fixed-$u$ asymptotic $\#\{p\le x:P^+(p-1)\le x^{1/u}\}\sim\pi(x)\rho(u)$, so a positive proportion of primes have $x^{\varepsilon}$-smooth predecessors for each fixed $\varepsilon>0$. No error terms or uniformity as $u$ grows are claimed. The companion on $\mu(p-1)=1$ (infinitely many primes with $p-1$ squarefree with an even number of prime factors) is linked here, not cataloged, since it cites no posing source.

fields.name: Erdős's totient-fiber conjecture: $\varphi(m)=n$ has more than $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ solutions for infinitely many $n$
fields.field: Multiplicative number theory; Euler's totient function
fields.statement: Let $g(n)=\#\{m\ge1:\varphi(m)=n\}$ count the preimages of $n$ under Euler's totient function. An elementary bound gives $g(n)\ll_\eta n^{1+\eta}$; Pillai showed $\limsup g(n)=\infty$ and Erdős (1935) showed $g(n)>n^c$ infinitely often for some $c>0$. Pomerance (1980) formulated the question as whether the supremum $C$ of exponents with $g(n)>n^c$ infinitely often equals $1$, attributing it to Erdős, and showed it would follow from enough primes $p$ whose predecessor $p-1$ has no prime factor above $p^\varepsilon$. The best exponent known was $0.7157$ (Lichtman 2022), after Baker-Harman's $0.7039$. Is it true that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are infinitely many $n$ with $g(n)>n^{1-\varepsilon}$?
fields.posedBy: Paul Erdős (1956, as attributed by Pomerance 1980); Erdős Problem #821
fields.ageNote: The manuscript follows Pomerance (1980, p. 84), who attributes the conjecture to Erdős (1956); erdosproblems.com lists it as Problem #821 citing Erdős (1974). Erdős's work on totient multiplicities and smooth shifted primes goes back to 1935.

The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. This manuscript proves the smooth shifted-prime count and the totient consequence; its graph and kernel estimates are reused by the Poisson-Dirichlet companion (separate entry for the Ford-Konyagin-Luca conjecture).
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. The deduction from smooth shifted primes to large fibers is the classical Erdős-Pomerance argument (Pomerance's Theorem B), written out in full; the new input is the $x^{1-o(1)}$ count of primes with $x^\delta$-smooth predecessors, which goes far beyond the previous exponent 0.2843 and should be treated as unverified until specialists examine it. Not refereed here.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are infinitely many $n$ with $g(n)>n^{1-\varepsilon}$, which is optimal in the exponent because $g(n)\ll_\eta n^{1+\eta}$. The input is Theorem 1.2: for fixed $0<\delta<1/4$, at least $x^{1-o(1)}$ primes $p\in(2x,5x]$ have $P^+(p-1)\le x^\delta$; in particular there are infinitely many primes with $P^+(p-1)\le p^\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. It does not give a positive proportion of such primes (that stronger statement is in the Poisson-Dirichlet companion), and the $o(1)$ is not made explicit.

fields.name: The Erdős-Faudree-Rousseau-Schelp cycle-clique conjecture: $R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1$ for $m\ge n\ge3$
fields.field: Graph Ramsey theory
fields.statement: Let $R(C_m,K_n)$ be the least $N$ such that every red-blue colouring of the edges of $K_N$ contains a red cycle of length exactly $m$ or a blue $K_n$. Taking $n-1$ disjoint red cliques of order $m-1$ with all edges between them blue gives $R(C_m,K_n)\ge(m-1)(n-1)+1$. Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp (1978) conjectured equality for $m\ge n\ge3$, apart from $R(C_3,K_3)=6$. Bondy and Erdős proved it for $m\ge n^2-2$, Nikiforov for $m\ge4n+2$, it was settled for $n\le7$, and Keevash, Long and Skokan (2021) proved it for $m\ge C\log n/\log\log n$ with an unspecified absolute constant, leaving finitely many pairs that could not be listed. Is $R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1$ for all $m\ge n\ge3$ with $(m,n)\ne(3,3)$?
fields.posedBy: Paul Erdős, Ralph Faudree, Cecil Rousseau and Richard Schelp (J. Graph Theory 1978); Erdős Problem #551
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results in the release were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with one fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This family is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The proof is computer-assisted: a structural reduction leaves 3,099 finite parameter-pattern instances, which accompanying programs exclude with deduction traces. The release also contains a Lean formalization of the full theorem.

The statement was read here: for all integers $3\le n\le m$ with $(m,n)\ne(3,3)$ the least $N$ such that every graph on $N$ vertices contains a copy of the $m$-cycle or its complement contains $K_n$ equals $(m-1)(n-1)+1$, and the value at $(3,3)$ is 6. That is the headline claim, including the finitely many computer-checked cases. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1: $R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1$ for every $m\ge n\ge3$ other than $(3,3)$, where $R(C_3,K_3)=6$. The proof takes a minimal counterexample (independent sets expand), finds a clique of order at least $\max\{3,\lfloor k/2\rfloor\}$, optimizes path systems between clique vertices, and reduces the rest to 3,099 finite instances excluded by two exact programs. Keevash-Long-Skokan had already left only finitely many pairs open, without an explicit list; this result closes all of them. It does not address the side questions recorded with Problem #551 for fixed $n$ (the least cycle length at which the identity holds when $m<n$ is allowed, and the minimum of $R(C_k,K_n)$ over $k$).

fields.name: Foulkes' conjecture for the sixth symmetric power: $\mathrm{Sym}^6(\mathrm{Sym}^bV)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Sym}^b(\mathrm{Sym}^6V)$
fields.field: Representation theory; plethysm
fields.statement: For a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ and integers $1\le a\le b$, Foulkes' conjecture (1950) asks for a $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-equivariant injection $\mathrm{Sym}^a(\mathrm{Sym}^bV)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Sym}^b(\mathrm{Sym}^aV)$, equivalently that the plethysm difference $h_b[h_a]-h_a[h_b]$ is Schur-positive. It was known for $a\le5$: $a=2$ from Thrall, $a=3$ by Dent-Siemons, $a=4$ and $a=5$ from McKay's propagation theorem with computations by Müller-Neunhöffer and Cheung-Ikenmeyer-Mkrtchyan. Brion proved it for $b$ large in terms of $a$, and Evseev-Paget-Wildon checked $a+b\le19$. The canonical Foulkes-Howe map has a kernel at $(6,6)$, so the propagation route fails at $a=6$. For $a=6$, is there an equivariant injection $\mathrm{Sym}^6(\mathrm{Sym}^bV)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Sym}^b(\mathrm{Sym}^6V)$ for every $b\ge6$ and every $V$?
fields.posedBy: H. O. Foulkes (J. London Math. Soc. 1950)
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results in the release were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with one fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This family is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The proof combines the companion's quadratic-stabilization theorem (range b >= 30) with certified multiplicity comparisons computed by printed programs for 6 <= b <= 29; a second, longer route runs the certificates through b = 149 and uses a chart bound beyond.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 and the introduction were read against Foulkes' conjecture as the manuscript states it. Lean: lean/docs/210.md covers only the companion (challenge FoulkesHowe, theorem OAI.Problem346.canonical_foulkes_howe_surjective, in formalization.yaml). Its statement gives surjectivity of the canonical map for $b\ge a(a-1)$, so for $a=6$ only $b\ge30$, and states surjectivity rather than the embedding; the docs say the companion's full range $b\ge6$ is not included. So the formal statement covers a special range, not this entry's headline, and the tier stays unreviewed. The band $6\le b\le29$ rests on computer certificates that were not rerun here. Not refereed.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $b\ge6$ and every finite-dimensional complex $V$ there is a $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-equivariant injection $\mathrm{Sym}^6(\mathrm{Sym}^bV)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Sym}^b(\mathrm{Sym}^6V)$, i.e. $h_b[h_6]-h_6[h_b]$ is Schur-positive. The range $b\ge30$ comes from the companion's quadratic stabilization theorem; $6\le b\le29$ is settled by certified comparisons of upper bounds for source multiplicities with lower bounds for target multiplicities. It proves the multiplicity comparison, not injectivity of the canonical map (which fails at $(6,6)$), and only the case $a=6$; Foulkes' conjecture for $a\ge7$ and $b<a(a-1)$ stays open.

fields.name: Landsberg's Problem 7.19: a polynomial stabilization bound for the canonical Foulkes-Howe map
fields.field: Representation theory; Chow varieties and geometric complexity theory
fields.statement: For $a,b\ge1$ and a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, the canonical Foulkes-Howe (Hadamard-Howe) map $\mu_{a,b,V}:\mathrm{Sym}^b(\mathrm{Sym}^aV)\to\mathrm{Sym}^a(\mathrm{Sym}^bV)$ is induced by multiplication in $(\mathrm{Sym}V)^{\otimes a}$; its image is the degree-$b$ part of the coordinate ring of the Chow variety of products of $a$ linear forms, whose normalization is the whole target. Surjectivity in degree $b$ gives an equivariant embedding as in Foulkes' conjecture. Brion proved eventual surjectivity and later an effective bound depending on both $a$ and $\dim V$. Landsberg's survey of geometric complexity theory (Problem 7.19) asks for a polynomial bound. Is there a degree bound, polynomial in $a$ and valid in every dimension, beyond which $\mu_{a,b,V}$ is surjective?
fields.posedBy: J. M. Landsberg (Geometric complexity theory: an introduction for geometers, Ann. Univ. Ferrara 2015, Problem 7.19)
fields.ageNote: Cited from the published 2015 version (arXiv:1305.7387, 2013). The underlying stabilization question goes back to Brion (1993, 1997).
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results in the release were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with one fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This family is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The stabilization theorem is also the large-degree input to the companion proving the sixth case of Foulkes' conjecture (separate entry). The release includes a Lean formalization of it.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1 and the history paragraph were read against Landsberg's request for a polynomial bound as the manuscript cites it. Lean: formalization.yaml lists ComparatorChallenges/FoulkesHowe (declaration OAI.Problem346.canonical_foulkes_howe_surjective, file OAI/RepresentationTheory/FoulkesHowe/Stabilization.lean). The statement was read: for every finite-dimensional complex $V$ and $a\ge2$, $b\ge a(a-1)$, there is a unique linear map given by the averaged transpose formula on products, and it is surjective. That is the headline. Not rebuilt here. The paper does not claim the bound is sharp.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1: for every $a\ge2$, $b\ge a(a-1)$ and finite-dimensional complex $V$, $\mu_{a,b,V}$ is surjective; equivalently the Chow-variety coordinate ring agrees with its normalization in degree $b$. In Landsberg's notation the bound is $d\ge n(n-1)$, in every dimension. By complete reducibility this yields Foulkes' embedding $\mathrm{Sym}^a(\mathrm{Sym}^bV)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Sym}^b(\mathrm{Sym}^aV)$ for $b\ge a(a-1)$. The least stabilization degree is not determined, the bound is not claimed sharp, and nothing is said about injectivity of the map in the other direction (which fails at $(5,5)$ and $(6,6)$).

fields.name: The Sharan-Sidford-Valiant precision question: do learners with $o(d^2)$ memory need $\Omega(d\log(1/\epsilon))$ samples for linear regression?
fields.field: Learning theory; memory-sample tradeoffs
fields.statement: A streaming learner sees pairs $(x_t,y_t)$ with independent rows $x_t\sim N(0,I_d)$ and labels $y_t=\langle x_t,s\rangle$ for an unknown unit vector $s$, reads each pair once and keeps at most $M$ bits between samples. With enough memory to store the equations, about $d$ samples determine $s$; with real registers, Kaczmarz projection reaches accuracy $\epsilon$ after about $d\log(1/\epsilon)$ samples. Building on Raz's memory-sample lower bounds for parity, Sharan, Sidford and Valiant (STOC 2019) showed that $d^2/4$ bits force $\Omega(d\log\log(1/\epsilon))$ samples in a noisy version of this experiment, and asked (Section 1.1) whether the first-order dependence of the sample count on the precision is optimal under bounded memory. Must every learner with $o(d^2)$ (or at most $Ad^2$) bits of memory use $\Omega(d\log(1/\epsilon))$ samples to estimate $s$ to accuracy $\epsilon$?
fields.posedBy: Vatsal Sharan, Aaron Sidford and Gregory Valiant (Memory-sample tradeoffs for linear regression with small error, STOC 2019, Section 1.1)
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results in the release were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with one fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This family is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family has six manuscripts of the same date: the principal one proves the lower bound for memory up to $Ad^2$, and five companions give alternative proofs or supporting estimates (posterior replicas, subsphere methods, projection moments and cap domination, Gaussian replacement, localization and information growth). Most are partly formalized in Lean.

Checked here: the main theorem, its two corollaries and the predecessors section of the principal manuscript were read against the Sharan-Sidford-Valiant question as the manuscript cites it. Lean: lean/docs/140.md lists eight challenges. ComparatorChallenges/NoiselessRegression (theorem OAI.NoiselessRegression.main, solution module OAI.Probability.GaussianRegression.Main, file exists at the pinned commit) is not in formalization.yaml; its statement was read here: for $M=o(d^2)$ an absolute $c$ with $T\ge c\,d\log(1/\epsilon)$ under uniform-prior or every-signal success $2/3$, and for $M\le Ad^2$ a constant $c_A$, for finite-state randomized learners with exact Gaussian observations and angular error. That is the headline. MemoryPrecision.main (in formalization.yaml) covers supporting estimates and the $M\le d^2$ case. Not rebuilt here. The model is exact (noiseless) observations; the noisy consequence is derived in the paper, not formalized.
fields.resultNote: Main theorem: for fixed $A>0$ there are $c_A,d_A$ such that any learner with $M\le Ad^2$ bits, $d\ge d_A$, $0<\epsilon\le1/10$ and uniform-prior success at least $2/3$ in reaching angular error $\epsilon$ needs horizon $T\ge c_A d\log(1/\epsilon)$; for $M=o(d^2)$ the constant is absolute, and the bound also holds under an every-signal guarantee. Transitions may use unbounded computation and randomness; the output uses only the terminal state, stopping index and fresh randomness, with a deterministic horizon. It implies an $\Omega_A(dr\log d)$ bound in the noisy experiment of Sharan-Sidford-Valiant at Euclidean accuracy $d^{-r}$ in their range. No matching finite-memory upper bound is proved, and memory well above $d^2$ is not treated.

fields.name: Berkholz's question: is Weisfeiler-Leman equivalence with the dimension as part of the input EXPTIME-complete?
fields.field: Computational complexity; graph isomorphism and finite model theory
fields.statement: The $k$-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm repeatedly refines colours of $k$-tuples of vertices; two graphs are $k$-WL equivalent if their stable colour histograms agree. For fixed $k$ this takes time $n^{O(k)}$, so with $k$ given in binary the equivalence problem lies in EXPTIME. Seppelt (MFCS 2024), and independently Lichter, Rassmann and Schweitzer, proved it coNP-hard when $k$ is part of the input, and Seppelt recorded Christoph Berkholz's question whether it is in fact EXPTIME-complete. Given two graphs by adjacency matrices and a dimension $k\ge2$ in binary, is deciding $k$-WL equivalence EXPTIME-complete?
fields.posedBy: Christoph Berkholz, as recorded by Tim Seppelt (MFCS 2024, the question preceding Theorem 5)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites the question only through Seppelt (2024); when Berkholz first raised it is not stated.

The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family has four manuscripts of the same date sharing a compressed-computation construction: the principal one (variable-dimension equivalence), graph identification with dimension in the input, unconditional fixed-dimension time lower bounds, and parity lifts with ETH-based exclusions. All four main statements are formalized in Lean.

fields.name: Schramm's Problem 2.3: Gaussian free field and SLE$_4$ limits of uniform real Lipschitz heights on the triangular lattice
fields.field: Statistical mechanics; random surfaces and SLE
fields.statement: Let $D$ be a smooth simply connected planar domain with two marked boundary points splitting its boundary into arcs $A_+$ and $A_-$, approximated by triangular-lattice polygons of mesh $\delta$. Sample real heights on the vertices uniformly (Lebesgue measure) subject to $|h(x)-h(y)|\le1$ across every edge, with boundary values $+\lambda$ on $A_+$ and $-\lambda$ on $A_-$. This hard-constraint gradient model lies outside the uniformly convex potentials covered by Schramm-Sheffield and Miller. In his ICM 2006 problem collection Schramm asked (Problem 2.3) for its scaling limits: a Gaussian free field for the height and SLE$_4$ for the zero-height interface at a suitable boundary amplitude; Problem 2.2 asks the analogous questions for uniform odd integer heights with increments $0,\pm2$. As $\delta\to0$, does the height converge to a multiple of the Dirichlet Gaussian free field, and does the zero interface converge to chordal SLE$_4$ for a tuned $\lambda$?
fields.posedBy: Oded Schramm (Conformally invariant scaling limits: an overview and a collection of problems, ICM 2006, Problems 2.2 and 2.3)
fields.ageNote: Posed in Schramm's ICM 2006 (Madrid) lecture, published in the Proceedings in 2007.

The family has three manuscripts of the same date: the principal one on real heights (Problem 2.3), one on the field part of Problem 2.2 for odd integer heights, and one on weighted integer heights (loop O(2) model).

fields.name: Erdős and Prachar's question: do the increases of $p_n/n$ have positive lower density?
fields.field: Distribution of prime gaps
fields.statement: Let $p_n$ be the $n$th prime and $u_n=p_n/n$. Erdős and Prachar (1962) proved $\sum_{p_n<x}|u_{n+1}-u_n|\asymp(\log x)^2$ and that the set of $n$ with $u_n>u_{n+1}$ has positive density, and asked about the reverse inequality. Since $u_n<u_{n+1}$ is equivalent to $p_{n+1}-p_n>p_n/n\sim\log p_n$, the question asks whether a positive proportion of prime gaps exceed the average gap, which needs control of how often gaps are large rather than of the largest gaps. Positive proportions were known only for gaps above a fixed fraction (about $0.579$) of $\log p_n$. Does the set of $n$ with $p_n/n<p_{n+1}/(n+1)$ have positive lower density?
fields.posedBy: Paul Erdős and Karl Prachar (Abh. Math. Sem. Univ. Hamburg 1962, p. 256); Erdős Problem #968
fields.ageNote: erdosproblems.com cites Erdős (1965) for the question and Erdős-Prachar for the background results; the manuscript cites the Erdős-Prachar paper, dated 1962.

The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The release also formalizes both the main theorem and the corollary in Lean.

The statement was read: for every $C>0$ there are $c>0$ and $N_0$ with at least $cN$ indices $n\le N$ having $p_{n+1}-p_n>C\log p_n$ for all $N\ge N_0$, and the set of $n$ with $p_n/n<p_{n+1}/(n+1)$ has positive lower asymptotic density. That is the headline. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every fixed $C>0$ there are $c(C)>0$ and $N_0(C)$ with $\#\{n\le N:p_{n+1}-p_n>C\log p_n\}\ge c(C)N$ for all $N\ge N_0$, with ordinary lower density and equal weight on prime indices. Corollary 1.2 (take $C=2$) answers Erdős-Prachar: the increases of $p_n/n$ have positive lower density. The main theorem is stronger than the posed question. The constant $c(C)$ is not made explicit or compared with the Poisson prediction $e^{-C}$, and the further questions recorded with Problem #968 on $u_n<u_{n+1}<u_{n+2}$ and $u_n>u_{n+1}>u_{n+2}$ are not addressed.

fields.name: The Gopalan-Servedio conjecture: is $\sum_i\widehat f(\{i\})=O(\sqrt{\deg f})$ for Boolean functions?
fields.field: Analysis of Boolean functions
fields.statement: For $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ write $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E[f(X)\prod_{i\in S}X_i]$ with $X$ uniform, and let $\deg f$ be the degree of its real multilinear representation. Cauchy-Schwarz gives $\sum_i\widehat f(\{i\})=\mathbb E[f(X)\sum_iX_i]\le\sqrt n$, attained up to constants by majority, while total influence gives $\sum_i|\widehat f(\{i\})|\le\deg f$. Gopalan and Servedio conjectured, around 2009, that $\sqrt n$ can be replaced by $\sqrt{\deg f}$; the conjecture is recorded in O'Donnell's list of open problems in analysis of Boolean functions and as Conjecture 3.17 of Filmus, Hatami, Keller and Lifshitz. A sharper majority-benchmark version was refuted at degree 4 by Kudin and Pasalic, which does not decide the square-root form. Is there an absolute constant $C$ with $\sum_i\widehat f(\{i\})\le C\sqrt{\deg f}$ for every Boolean function $f$?
fields.posedBy: Parikshit Gopalan and Rocco Servedio (c. 2009), recorded in O'Donnell's Open Problems in Analysis of Boolean Functions (2012, p. 9)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript attributes the conjecture to Gopalan and Servedio circa 2009 via O'Donnell's 2012 problem list; no dated original source is cited.

The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The release also formalizes the disproof in Lean.

The statement was read: for every $C>0$ there is a nonconstant $\pm1$-valued function on a finite sign cube with $C\sqrt{\deg f}$ below the sum of its singleton Fourier coefficients, where degree is the real Fourier degree, and the ratio of the absolute singleton sum to $\sqrt{\deg f}$ is unbounded. That is the headline. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1: for every $C>0$ there is a nonconstant $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ with $\sum_i\widehat f(\{i\})>C\sqrt{\deg f}$; equivalently $\sum_i|\widehat f(\{i\})|/\sqrt{\deg f}$ is unbounded over Boolean functions of positive degree, so no constant multiple of the conjectured bound holds. The dimension and copy counts in the construction are finite but not usefully bounded, so no growth rate of the violation in terms of degree is given. The true order between $\sqrt{\deg f}$ and the linear bound $\deg f$ is left open.

fields.name: Ball's extension problem for Lipschitz maps from Hilbert space into $\ell_1$, via the Mendel-Naor metric Markov cotype question
fields.field: Metric geometry; nonlinear Banach space theory, Lipschitz extension
fields.statement: Ball (1992) introduced Markov type and cotype to study Lipschitz extension and asked whether every Lipschitz map $f$ from an arbitrary subset of a Hilbert space $H$ into $L_1$ extends to all of $H$ with $\mathrm{Lip}(F)\le K\,\mathrm{Lip}(f)$ for a universal $K$. Mendel and Naor (2013) formulated metric Markov cotype two in Cesaro form: $X$ has it with constant $C$ if for every reversible stochastic matrix $A$ with stationary $\pi$, every $t$ and points $x_1,\dots,x_n\in X$ there are $y_1,\dots,y_n\in X$ with $\sum_i\pi_i d(x_i,y_i)^2+t\sum_{i,j}\pi_i a_{ij}d(y_i,y_j)^2\le C^2\sum_{i,j}\pi_i(\frac1t\sum_{s=1}^tA^s)_{ij}d(x_i,x_j)^2$. They showed that a positive answer for $\ell_1$ yields the extension, and asked (Question 1.15): is $N_2(\ell_1)<\infty$, that is, does $\ell_1$ have metric Markov cotype two?
fields.posedBy: Keith Ball (1992, extension problem); Manor Mendel and Assaf Naor (2013, Question 1.15)
fields.ageNote: Ball's extension problem dates from his 1992 GAFA paper 'Markov chains, Riesz transforms and Lipschitz maps'. The metric Markov cotype question for l1 was asked explicitly by Mendel and Naor in 2013 (Analysis and Geometry in Metric Spaces, Question 1.15 and Section 7). The paper also cites Naor-Young (Acta Math. 2022) for discussion of the extension problem.

The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. It is a single paper; the extension theorem is derived as a corollary by combining the main theorem with Mendel and Naor's published extension theorem.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the abstract, introduction, Theorem 1.1 and the final section of the TeX source were read against Ball's problem and Mendel-Naor Question 1.15. The paper proves $N_2(\ell_1)\le12\sqrt{21}$ directly and obtains the extension corollary by invoking Mendel-Naor Corollary 1.13, so the extension relies on that published theorem. The family has no Lean formalization (lean/docs/332.md does not exist at the pinned commit). The target is real (and, by a corollary, complex) $\ell_1$; the paper says 'for this target' and does not discuss general $L_1(\mu)$ targets.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: real $\ell_1$ has metric Markov cotype two with $N_2(\ell_1)\le12\sqrt{21}$, uniformly in the number of points, coordinates and time parameter; complex $\ell_1$ follows with $12\sqrt{42}$. Corollary: there is a universal $K$ such that every Lipschitz $f:S\to\ell_1$, $S$ any subset of a real Hilbert space, extends to $F:H\to\ell_1$ with $\mathrm{Lip}(F)\le K\,\mathrm{Lip}(f)$. The construction is nonlinear (expected coordinatewise medians of geometric-walk endpoints after cut smoothing), consistent with the known failure of Ball's linear Markov cotype for $\ell_1$ and the Kalton-based subspace counterexample. No optimal constant is claimed, and targets other than $\ell_1$ are not treated.
fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Metric Markov Cotype Two of l1
fields.significanceNote: Ball's Hilbert-to-L1 extension problem is a central open question of nonlinear Banach space theory, open since 1992; famous within metric geometry, unknown outside it. Placed level with Naor's sublinear-dimension question for finite subsets of Lp (35), just below The Lang-Plaut problem (38) and just above Talagrand's operator cotype problem (32).

fields.name: Kirchberg-Rordam comparison question: pure infiniteness implies strong pure infiniteness, and weak equals strong for exact C*-algebras
fields.field: Operator algebras; C*-algebras, pure infiniteness
fields.statement: Kirchberg and Rordam introduced three notions for (possibly nonsimple) C*-algebras: $C$ is purely infinite if every positive element $h$ is properly infinite ($h\oplus h\precsim h$ in Cuntz comparison), weakly purely infinite if $h^{\oplus n}$ is properly infinite for every positive $h$ and one fixed $n$, and strongly purely infinite if for all positive $x,y$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there are $s,t$ with $\|s^*x^2s-x^2\|<\varepsilon$, $\|t^*y^2t-y^2\|<\varepsilon$, $\|s^*xyt\|<\varepsilon$. Strong implies ordinary implies weak, and for separable nuclear algebras strong pure infiniteness is tied to $\mathcal O_\infty$-absorption. Do the three notions coincide, in general and for nuclear algebras?
fields.posedBy: Eberhard Kirchberg and Mikael Rordam (Adv. Math. 2002, Question 9.5); recorded as Problem LXXII by Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White
fields.ageNote: The notions were introduced in Kirchberg-Rordam, 'Infinite non-simple C*-algebras: absorbing the Cuntz algebra O-infinity' (Adv. Math. 167, 2002). The question is restated in Schafhauser-Tikuisis-White, 'Nuclear C*-algebras: 99 problems' (arXiv 2506.10902, Section 21, Problem LXXII).

Both solution files exist at the pinned commit; neither challenge is in the formalization catalogue formalization.yaml. The statements were read here: for a nonunital complex C*-algebra, every positive element properly infinite (Cuntz comparison in a stabilization built in the file) implies arbitrary-entry diagonalization and strong pure infiniteness; for exact algebras (exactness defined from scratch in the file) weak pure infiniteness implies strong. That is the headline. Not rebuilt here. The O-infinity absorption corollary rests on published Kirchberg results and is not formalized.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every complex C*-algebra in which every positive element is properly infinite is strongly purely infinite, with an arbitrary cross term in the diagonalization. Theorem 1.2: for exact algebras, proper infiniteness of $h^{\oplus n}$ for one fixed $n$ and all positive $h$ implies proper infiniteness of every positive element, hence strong pure infiniteness. Corollary: a separable nuclear algebra with this fixed-amplification property absorbs $\mathcal O_\infty$, with no unitality or simplicity assumption (via Kirchberg's central-sequence results). Not settled: whether weak pure infiniteness implies pure infiniteness for non-exact algebras, which the paper states remains outside its conclusions.

fields.significanceNote: Whether pure infiniteness implies strong pure infiniteness has been a recognized open question in the theory of nonsimple purely infinite C*-algebras for over twenty years and is listed among the 99 problems on nuclear C*-algebras. Specialist but central there; the non-exact weak-to-ordinary part stays open. Placed just above Robert-Tikuisis Conjecture (C1) (25) and Szabo's Conjecture A in the unital stably finite case (22), far below Kadison's Similarity Problem (58).

fields.name: Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture
fields.field: Additive number theory; sumsets and the primes
fields.statement: Two subsets of $\mathbb N_0$ are asymptotically equal if their symmetric difference is finite. Ostmann conjectured that the set $\mathcal P$ of primes is asymptotically additively indecomposable. Is it true that there are no sets $A,B\subseteq\mathbb N_0$, each with at least two elements, such that $A+B$ differs from $\mathcal P$ in only finitely many elements?
fields.posedBy: Hans-Heinrich Ostmann (Additive Zahlentheorie, 1956, p. 13); restated by Elsholtz and Harper (2015, Conjecture 1.2)
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model using one fixed procedure, about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result on average. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the introduction and Theorem 1.1 were read against Ostmann's conjecture. lean/docs/013.md lists OstmannPrimes.json (OAI.Ostmann.main, module OAI.NumberTheory.Ostmann.Main) and OstmannComplete.json (OAI.Ostmann.inverseGoldbach and OAI.Ostmann.twoInfiniteSummandsImpossible, module OAI.NumberTheory.Ostmann.Complete). Both solution files exist at the pinned commit; neither challenge is in the formalization catalogue formalization.yaml. The statement was read here: for all sets A, B of natural numbers with at least two elements each, the symmetric difference of A+B and the primes is infinite. That is exactly the conjecture. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if $A,B\subseteq\mathbb N_0$ have $|A|,|B|\ge2$, then $(A+B)\triangle\mathcal P$ is infinite. After the Laffer-Mann reduction to two infinite summands, the proof combines residue restrictions at every prime, decorrelation from translated multiplicative characters, prime coverage and a positive statistic averaged over arrangements; it does not use Green and Harper's conditional inverse-sieve route. In particular, if $A+B$ contains every large prime it contains infinitely many composites. No quantitative version is claimed.

fields.significanceNote: A named conjecture of additive number theory, open since 1956 and attacked with sieve methods by Hornfeck, Elsholtz, Green-Harper and Croot-Mao-Pohoata-Yip. fields.name: The $n^{1/6}$ free-energy fluctuation scale of the low-temperature Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, with a limiting law
fields.field: Spin glasses; Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model
fields.statement: In the zero-field Gaussian Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model $H_n(\sigma)=\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i<j}g_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j$, let $F_n=\log\sum_\sigma e^{\beta H_n(\sigma)}$. At high temperature $\beta<1$ the fluctuations of $F_n$ are of order one (Aizenman-Lebowitz-Ruelle). For fixed $\beta>1$, Crisanti, Paladin, Sommers and Vulpiani predicted that the free energy per spin fluctuates on the scale $n^{-5/6}$, that is $\mathrm{sd}(F_n)\asymp n^{1/6}$, and Parisi and Rizzo developed the related large-deviation calculation. Is the standard deviation of $F_n$ of order $n^{1/6}$ at every fixed $\beta>1$, and does the centered, rescaled free energy converge to a limiting law?
fields.posedBy: A. Crisanti, G. Paladin, H.-J. Sommers and A. Vulpiani (J. Phys. I France 2, 1992); developed by Parisi and Rizzo (2008-2009)
fields.ageNote: The prediction is in Crisanti-Paladin-Sommers-Vulpiani, 'Replica trick and fluctuations in disordered systems' (1992), following Kondor's 1983 replica expansion. The best rigorous bounds before this work were Aronow-Lopatto (2026): n^(4/15) <= Var F_n <= n^(7/15).

Results are for fixed beta > 1, zero field, Gaussian couplings and Ising spins; nothing is claimed uniformly as beta tends to 1 or infinity, and the limiting law is characterized only by its moments, not identified with a named distribution.
fields.resultNote: Companion (fluctuation scale): for every fixed $\beta>1$, $\mathrm{sd}(F_n)=n^{1/6+o(1)}$ and $|F_n-\mathbb EF_n|$ is typically between $n^{1/6-\eta}$ and $n^{1/6+\eta}$. Principal (limiting law): $\mathrm{Var}(F_n)/n^{1/3}$ converges to a constant in $(0,\infty)$, every moment of the $n^{-1/6}$-rescaled completed free energy converges with a polynomial rate, exponential moments are uniformly bounded, and $(F_n-\mathbb EF_n)/\mathrm{sd}(F_n)$ converges along all $n$ to a nondegenerate law with mean 0 and variance 1, uniquely determined by its moments. The law is not identified with a named distribution and no formula for the variance constant is given.

fields.name: Optimal-order mixing of the Thorp shuffle on $2^d$ cards: is the mixing time $O(\log n)$?
fields.field: Markov chain mixing times; card shuffling
fields.statement: The Thorp shuffle on $n=2^d$ cards cuts the deck into two halves, pairs the cards in corresponding positions, orders each pair by an independent fair coin, and interleaves the pairs. Each card is uniform after $d$ shuffles and a counting argument gives a lower bound of order $d$ for the whole permutation, while the known upper bounds were $O(d^{44})$ (Morris 2008), $O(d^{29})$ (Montenegro-Tetali) and $O(d^3)$ (Morris 2013). Is the total-variation mixing time of the full permutation $O(d)=O(\log n)$?

fields.name: The one-dimensional Lieb-Thirring conjecture for $1/2<\gamma<3/2$
fields.field: Spectral theory; sharp Lieb-Thirring constants
fields.statement: For $0\le W\in L^{\gamma+1/2}(\mathbb R)$ the Lieb-Thirring inequality reads $\sum_j|\lambda_j(-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}-W)|^\gamma\le L_{\gamma,1}\int_{\mathbb R}W^{\gamma+1/2}$. The sharp constant is the semiclassical one for $\gamma\ge3/2$ (Lieb-Thirring, Aizenman-Lieb) and equals $1/2$ at $\gamma=1/2$ (Hundertmark-Lieb-Thomas). For $1/2<\gamma<3/2$, Lieb and Thirring conjectured that the optimal constant equals the one-bound-state constant $L^{(1)}_{\gamma,1}$, the best constant when only the lowest eigenvalue is counted. Is $L_{\gamma,1}=L^{(1)}_{\gamma,1}$ for every $1/2<\gamma<3/2$?

fields.ageNote: Conjecture from Lieb-Thirring, 'Inequalities for the moments of the eigenvalues of the Schrodinger Hamiltonian and their relation to Sobolev inequalities' (Bargmann Festschrift, 1976). The case gamma = 1 was proved by Read and Schulz (2026) before this work; the paper claims the remaining cases.

fields.name: Williams's one-tape question: simulating one-tape time $T$ in $O(T^{1/2-\delta})$ space
fields.field: Computational complexity; time-space simulation
fields.statement: A classical simulation (attributed to Hopcroft and Ullman) computes the outcome of a deterministic one-tape Turing machine running for $T$ steps in $O(\sqrt T)$ space, with unrestricted simulation time. Simulation time is unrestricted, the final tape is not materialized, no lower bound or optimality is claimed, and for several writable tapes only $O(\sqrt T\,\mathrm{polylog})$ is given.

fields.name: The Alcalde Lopez-Heeney-Lis conjecture: joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller heights and current clusters
fields.field: Statistical mechanics; conformally invariant scaling limits
fields.statement: On the critical line of the Ashkin-Teller model ($J>0$, $U\le J$, $\sinh 2J=e^{-2U}$), Lis's representation gives a height function and primal and dual current-cluster collections. fields.name: Litt's potential integral density question for $\mathrm{SL}_r$ character varieties of curves
fields.shortName: Litt's integral density question for curves
fields.field: Arithmetic geometry; character varieties, integral points
fields.statement: For a smooth complex variety $X$, the $\mathrm{SL}_r$-character variety of $\pi_1(X)$ has a natural model $M_r(X)$ over $\mathbb Z$. Litt asked whether integral points on such character varieties become Zariski dense after a finite extension of the ground field, including a variant with prescribed boundary monodromy, and whether one number field $L$ suffices so that the points over the full ring of integers $\mathcal O_L$ are dense in every component. Coccia and Litt proved this for $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ and conjectured it for Chevalley groups with fixed boundary data. For a smooth connected curve $X$, every rank $r$ and prescribed quasi-unipotent boundary classes, is there one number field over whose full ring of integers the integral points are Zariski dense?

fields.name: Gromov's codimension-two Urysohn width conjecture for positive scalar curvature, with the macroscopic dimension conjecture for universal covers
fields.field: Scalar curvature; Urysohn width and macroscopic dimension
fields.statement: For a metric space $X$ the Urysohn $d$-width $\mathrm{UW}_d(X)$ is the infimum, over continuous maps $f:X\to K$ to simplicial complexes of dimension at most $d$, of $\sup_y\operatorname{diam}f^{-1}(y)$. Gromov proposed that positive scalar curvature collapses two dimensions at the curvature scale: a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold with $\mathrm{Scal}\ge1$ should map to an $(n-2)$-dimensional polyhedron with all point inverses of diameter bounded by a constant depending only on $n$, and the universal cover of a closed manifold with positive scalar curvature should have macroscopic dimension at most $n-2$. Known: closed and complete three-manifolds (Gromov-Lawson, Liokumovich-Maximo, Liokumovich-Wang), spin cases under the Strong Novikov Conjecture (Bolotov, Bolotov-Dranishnikov), and the aspherical consequence in dimensions four and five (Chodosh-Li, Gromov). Is $\mathrm{UW}_{n-2}(M)\le C_n$ for every complete $n$-manifold with $\mathrm{Scal}\ge1$?
fields.posedBy: Mikhael Gromov (Large Riemannian manifolds, 1986, Section 2.A(c); Positive curvature, macroscopic dimension, spectral gaps and higher signatures, 1996, Section 2 1/2; A dozen problems, 2017)
fields.ageNote: The spectral companion dates the quantitative formulation to Gromov 1986, Section 2.A(c); the principal manuscript cites the 1996 macroscopic-dimension paper and Gromov's 2017 problem list (filling-radius Conjecture A-minus).

fields.name: The Kollar-Pardon conjecture on projective varieties with semialgebraic universal cover
fields.field: Complex algebraic geometry; universal covers and uniformization
fields.statement: In dimension one uniformization leaves only $\mathbb P^1$, $\mathbb C$ and the disc as universal covers. fields.name: Sharpness of the Kesten-Stigum reconstruction threshold for three-state symmetric and ferromagnetic four-state Potts channels on trees
fields.field: Broadcasting on trees; reconstruction and community detection
fields.statement: A root spin, uniform on $q$ states, is broadcast down a tree through a symmetric channel with second eigenvalue $\lambda$; reconstruction means the spins at depth $\ell$ keep non-vanishing information about the root. Kesten-Stigum gives reconstruction when $d\lambda^2>1$ ($d$ the branching number); Sly showed this is not sharp for $q\ge5$, and proved sharpness for $q=3$ on regular trees of large degree. Mezard and Montanari conjectured sharpness for three states (either sign of $\lambda$) and small alphabets, and discussed all branching parameters. For $q=3$ and for the ferromagnetic $q=4$ channel, on every regular tree and every Poisson Galton-Watson tree, is there non-reconstruction whenever $d\lambda^2\le1$?

fields.name: The Kirchberg-Rordam character question: does absence of characters on the central sequence algebra characterize Jiang-Su stability?
fields.field: Operator algebras; Jiang-Su stability and central sequences
fields.statement: For a nonzero unital separable C*-algebra $A$ and a free ultrafilter $\omega$, let $F_\omega(A)=A_\omega\cap A'$ be the norm central-sequence algebra. Kirchberg and Rordam proved $A\cong A\otimes\mathcal Z$ exactly when $F_\omega(A)$ contains, with the same unit, a separable subhomogeneous algebra without characters; absence of characters on $F_\omega(A)$ is then necessary. They asked (Question 3.1) whether it is sufficient, and related it to tensor powers (Question 3.7); the question reappears as Problem LXXX of Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White. Is $A$ Jiang-Su stable whenever $F_\omega(A)$ has no characters?
fields.posedBy: Eberhard Kirchberg and Mikael Rordam (When central sequence C*-algebras have characters, Internat. J. Math. 26 (2015), Questions 3.1 and 3.7); listed as Problem LXXX by Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White

fields.name: Harary's Snaky problem: is the Snaky hexomino a winner in the planar Maker-Breaker achievement game?
fields.field: Combinatorial games; polyomino achievement games
fields.statement: In Harary's polyomino achievement games two players alternately claim cells of the infinite square grid; Maker wins on owning a translated, rotated or reflected copy of a fixed polyomino. fields.name: Kohn-Sham ensemble v-representability of Coulomb ground-state densities by potentials in L^{3/2}+L^infinity
fields.field: Density functional theory; noninteracting v-representability
fields.statement: Kohn-Sham density functional theory replaces an interacting electronic ground state by noninteracting electrons in a common local potential that reproduces its density. Levy and Lieb separated the existence of states with a prescribed density from the existence of a potential for which such states are ground states; ensembles of degenerate noninteracting ground states enlarge the class (Ullrich-Kohn). Explicit non-representable model densities and numerical violations are known, but not for an actual Coulomb system. Is the ground-state density of every finite Coulomb molecule the density of a ground-state ensemble of noninteracting electrons in some real local potential $v\in L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^3)+L^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$?
fields.posedBy: Assumed by Kohn and Sham (1965); posed as the v-representability problem by Mel Levy (1979) and Elliott H. Lieb (Density functionals for Coulomb systems, 1983); reviewed by Penz et al. (2023)
fields.ageNote: The Kohn-Sham ansatz dates to 1965 and Levy's constrained search to 1979; 1983 is Lieb's formulation in the potential class used here.

No Lean formalization exists for this family. Scope limits stated by the paper: the counterexample uses nuclear separation $D=10^{200}$ in scaled units and a charge $Z$ given by an exact but non-numerical formula with no effective bound; it excludes only real spin-independent local potentials in $L^{3/2}+L^\infty$, and says nothing about distributional, spin-dependent or nonlocal potentials.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a finite positive integer $Z$ such that the three-electron Coulomb Hamiltonian with two nuclei of charge $Z$ at $\pm(D/Z)e_z$, $D=10^{200}$, has a normalizable absolute ground state $\Psi$ (sector $S_z=1/2$) whose spin-summed density is not the density of any ground-state ensemble of $H_s(v)$ for any real $v\in L^{3/2}+L^\infty$. The mechanism is the Gori-Giorgi-Gal-Baerends nodal-plane asymptotics, made rigorous, plus a kinetic certificate against all ensembles. A corollary rules out a local-potential first variation of the ensemble Hartree-exchange-correlation functional at that density. Not covered: larger potential classes, atoms, or physically realistic charges.
