fields.name: Bizeul's conjecture: a dimension-free log-Sobolev inequality for log-concave measures with subgaussian linear marginals
fields.field: Asymptotic convex geometry; functional inequalities for log-concave measures
fields.statement: Call a centered random vector $X$ linearly $a$-subgaussian if $\sup_{|\theta|=1}\mathbb E\exp(\langle X,\theta\rangle^2/a^2)\le2$. A log-Sobolev inequality forces such tails, and Bakry-Emery gives one under uniform convexity, but log-concavity alone does not. Bobkov's criterion gives a constant of order $na^2$ and Bizeul improved this to order $\sqrt n\,a^2$, with the dimension-free bound for rotationally invariant laws. Bizeul conjectured that subgaussian linear marginals suffice; Klartag and Lehec list it as Conjecture 76. Is there a universal $C$ such that every centered log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$ that is linearly $a$-subgaussian satisfies $\mathrm{Ent}_\mu(f^2)\le Ca^2\int|\nabla f|^2d\mu$?
fields.posedBy: Pierre Bizeul (On the log-Sobolev constant of log-concave vectors, formulated 2023, J. Funct. Anal. 290 (2026), Conjecture 2); Klartag and Lehec, Bull. AMS (2025), Conjecture 76

fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is an absolute $C$ such that for every $n$, every centered log-concave probability $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$ with a density and linear subgaussian parameter $a$, $\mathrm{Ent}_\mu(f^2)\le Ca^2\int|Df|^2d\mu$ for all $f\in C_c^\infty$; this includes uniform measures on convex bodies and needs no smoothness or curvature. By Otto-Villani it gives the transport-entropy inequality $W_2(\nu,\mu)^2\le Ca^2H(\nu|\mu)$ with the same constant. Not given: a value of $C$, or anything for non-log-concave measures.

fields.shortName: QAOA eventual Parisi optimality on SK
fields.field: Quantum optimization; spin glasses
fields.statement: For the zero-field Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model the expected QAOA energy per spin at fixed depth $p$ and fixed angles has an infinite-size limit $v_p(\gamma,\beta)$ (Farhi-Goldstone-Gutmann-Zhou), and $Q_p=\sup v_p$ cannot exceed the Parisi ground-state value $P_*$. fields.name: Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture: deforming hypersymplectic four-manifolds to hyperkahler triples in fixed cohomology
fields.field: Differential geometry: hypersymplectic and hyperkahler four-manifolds
fields.statement: A hypersymplectic structure on a closed oriented four-manifold $X$ is a triple $\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3)$ of closed two-forms whose pointwise span is three-dimensional and positive definite for the wedge product. Donaldson (2006, Section 5.3, Question 3) asked whether a compact oriented four-manifold carrying such a triple admits a hyperkahler structure, and proposed a continuity method keeping the cohomology classes fixed. Fine and Yao formulated the normalized deformation problem as a conjecture: after normalizing $\int_X\omega_i\wedge\omega_j=\delta_{ij}$, can every hypersymplectic triple be deformed through hypersymplectic triples, keeping each class $[\omega_i]$ fixed, to a hyperkahler triple, i.e. one with $\omega_i\wedge\omega_j=2\delta_{ij}\mu$ for a volume form $\mu$? Known before this work: convergence of the hypersymplectic flow for simple-type structures on $T^4$ (Huang-Wang-Yao), $T^3$-invariant triples on $T^4$ (Fine-He-Yao) and triples preserved by a circle action. Does every normalized hypersymplectic triple on a closed four-manifold deform, with its cohomology classes fixed, to a hyperkahler triple?
fields.posedBy: S. K. Donaldson, Two-forms on four-manifolds and elliptic equations (2006), Section 5.3, Question 3; deformation form stated as Conjecture 1.1 by J. Fine and C. Yao (Duke Math. J. 2018)
fields.ageNote: Donaldson's question appeared in the 2006 Chern memorial volume (arXiv math/0607083). The cohomology-preserving deformation statement is Fine and Yao's Conjecture 1.1 (arXiv 1704.07620, 2017; Duke Math. J. 167, 2018).

fields.name: The Hajlasz-Onninen endpoint question for the centered maximal function, planar disk case: is $\|\nabla Mf\|_1\le C\|\nabla f\|_1$ on $W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^2)$?
fields.field: Harmonic analysis: regularity of maximal functions
fields.statement:
For $f\in L^1_{loc}(\mathbb R^n)$ let $Mf(x)=\sup_{r>0}|B(x,r)|^{-1}\int_{B(x,r)}|f|$ be the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal function. Kinnunen proved that $M$ is bounded on $W^{1,p}$ for $1<p<\infty$, using $|
abla Mf|\le M|
abla f|$, but this argument fails at $p=1$ because $M$ is not bounded on $L^1$. Hajlasz and Onninen (2004, Question 1) asked whether the endpoint gradient bound nevertheless holds: is $f\mapsto|
abla Mf|$ bounded from $W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)$ to $L^1(\mathbb R^n)$? Known before this work: one dimension (Tanaka and Aldaz-Perez Lazaro for the uncentered operator, Kurka for the centered one), radial or block-decreasing inputs and the uncentered operator in higher dimensions (Luiro, Aldaz-Perez Lazaro), dyadic and uncentered-cube variants (Weigt), and fractional centered operators (Weigt). The centered operator in dimension at least two was open in general. In the plane, with disks: is there an absolute $C$ such that $\|
abla Mf\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^2)}\le C\|
abla f\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^2)}$ for every $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^2)$, with $Mf$ weakly differentiable?
fields.posedBy: P. Hajlasz and J. Onninen, On boundedness of maximal functions in Sobolev spaces, Ann. Acad. Sci. Fenn. Math. 29 (2004), Question 1
fields.ageNote: The question is posed in every dimension; this entry records only its planar centered-disk case, which the manuscript answers.

fields.name: Are all complex K3 surfaces Oka manifolds?
fields.field: Complex geometry: Oka theory and holomorphic flexibility
fields.statement: A complex manifold $X$ is Oka if maps from Stein manifolds to $X$ satisfy the Oka principle; by Forstneric's theorem this is equivalent to the convex approximation property: for every $m\ge1$, every holomorphic map to $X$ from a neighbourhood of a compact convex $K\subset\mathbb C^m$ can be approximated uniformly on $K$ by holomorphic maps $\mathbb C^m\to X$. Forstneric and Larusson's 2011 survey asked (Section 8, Problem C) whether K3 surfaces are Oka. Known before this work: elliptic and Kummer K3 surfaces are dominable by $\mathbb C^2$ (Buzzard-Lu), Kummer surfaces are strongly dominable, Kummer and elliptic K3 surfaces are Oka-1 (Alarcon-Forstneric), the Kobayashi pseudodistance vanishes on every K3 surface (Kamenova-Lu-Verbitsky), and Xie-Zhao proved that smooth $(2,2,2)$ hypersurfaces in $(\mathbb P^1)^3$ are Oka and that Oka K3 periods are dense, conjecturing that all K3 surfaces are Oka. Is every complex K3 surface, projective or not, an Oka manifold?

fields.name: Secret key from all entangled states: does every entangled state have positive distillable secret key? (Kruger-Werner Problem 24)
fields.shortName: Secret key from all entangled states
fields.field: Quantum cryptography: distillable secret key and bound entanglement
fields.statement: For a bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$, the distillable secret key $K_D(\rho)$ is the best rate at which Alice and Bob, using local operations and authenticated public communication on many copies, can extract bits that agree and are independent of an eavesdropper holding a purification and the public record. Separable states have $K_D=0$, and Horodecki et al. showed that some bound entangled (PPT) states nevertheless have $K_D>0$, so key and distillable entanglement differ. The converse was posed as Problem 24, 'Secret key from all entangled states', in Kruger and Werner's 2005 collection of open problems in quantum information theory (contact P. Horodecki). Is $K_D(\rho)>0$ for every entangled state $\rho$?

fields.ageNote: The open-problem entry is dated 15 March 2005 (arXiv quant-ph/0504166). The manuscript notes the question is also discussed in the private-state literature.

The theorem gives an explicit entangled state on $\mathbb C^{10}\otimes\mathbb C^{10}$ with $K_D=0$ for the paper's class of admitted protocols, which includes ordinary finite two-way public-discussion protocols with round counts growing with block length, plus specified countable processes; readers should note the answer is stated relative to that formal protocol model. The proof was not refereed. The release's Lean formalization (lean/docs/272.md) covers only the PPT-composition consequences, and says explicitly that the zero-key statement is outside it, so this entry is unreviewed. The state is the normalized Choi matrix of a composition of two PPT maps; a coherence inequality for such states bounds secrecy by disagreement probability. So the answer to Problem 24 is no. fields.name: The PPT-squared conjecture: is the composition of two PPT channels always entanglement breaking?
fields.field: Quantum channels: PPT maps and entanglement breaking
fields.statement: A linear map $F:M_a(\mathbb C)\to M_b(\mathbb C)$ is PPT if both $F$ and $T\circ F$ are completely positive, $T$ the transpose, and entanglement breaking if $(\mathrm{id}\otimes F)(X)$ is separable for every positive $X$, equivalently its Choi matrix is separable. Christandl conjectured that composing two PPT channels always yields an entanglement-breaking channel; the question was recorded as Problem G of the 2012 BIRS workshop 'Operator structures in quantum information theory', and stated for pairs of PPT maps as Conjecture IV.1 of Christandl, Muller-Hermes and Wolf (2019). fields.name: Gersten's conjecture for integral K-theory of arbitrary regular local rings (Quillen's form), in ramified mixed characteristic
fields.field: Algebraic K-theory of regular local rings
fields.statement: For a Noetherian regular local domain $A$ with fraction field $F$, Gersten's conjecture asserts exactness of the augmented complex $0\to K_n(A)\to K_n(F)\to\bigoplus_{\mathrm{ht}\,\mathfrak p=1}K_{n-1}(\kappa(\mathfrak p))\to\cdots$ of integral Quillen K-groups; its first assertion is that $K_n(A)\to K_n(F)$ is injective. Quillen formulated the conjecture for all regular local rings and proved it for regular local rings essentially of finite type over a field; Panin proved the full equicharacteristic case. In mixed characteristic it was known for rings smooth over a DVR modulo the DVR case (Gillet-Levine), with finite coefficients for rings essentially smooth over a DVR (Geisser-Levine) and for unramified regular local rings (Skalit), while Feld (2026) found a finite-coefficient failure at a ramified ring. Is $K_n(A)\to K_n(\mathrm{Frac}\,A)$ injective, and the Gersten complex exact, for every regular local ring $A$, including ramified rings of mixed characteristic?

fields.name: Villani's conjecture: weak Ma-Trudinger-Wang curvature implies convex tangent injectivity domains on compact manifolds
fields.field: Riemannian geometry and optimal transport regularity
fields.statement: Let $(M,g)$ be a compact connected Riemannian manifold without boundary, $c=d^2/2$, and $I(x)\subset T_xM$ the open tangent injectivity domain. The Ma-Trudinger-Wang tensor $\mathfrak S_{(x,v)}(\xi,\eta)$ is a fourth derivative of $c$; weak MTW (A3w) requires $\mathfrak S_{(x,v)}(\xi,\eta)\ge0$ whenever $\langle\xi,\eta\rangle=0$. Weak MTW is necessary for continuity of optimal transport maps (Loeper), and regularity theory (Figalli-Rifford-Villani) needed convex injectivity domains as an extra hypothesis. Villani proposed that weak MTW should by itself force convexity of every $I(x)$; Loeper-Villani proved convexity under strong MTW with nonfocality, and Figalli-Gallouet-Rifford proved the implication for nonfocal manifolds, where cut points come strictly before conjugate points. Does weak MTW imply that $I(x)$ is convex for every $x\in M$, with no nonfocality assumption?

fields.name: The Popa-Vaes paving conjecture over arbitrary maximal abelian subalgebras: strong-operator, approximation and quadratic paving
fields.field: Operator algebras: paving and maximal abelian subalgebras
fields.statement: Let $A\subseteq M$ be a maximal abelian $*$-subalgebra (MASA) of a von Neumann algebra. For a partition $P=(p_1,\dots,p_r)$ of $1$ in $A$ put $S_P(x)=\sum p_ixp_i$. After Marcus-Spielman-Srivastava solved Kadison-Singer paving for the diagonal MASA of $B(\ell^2)$, Popa and Vaes showed norm paving fails for general MASAs and introduced weaker notions: $x$ is so-pavable if $\|q(S_P(x)-a)q\|\le\varepsilon\|x\|$ for some $a\in A$ and a projection $q$ arbitrarily close to $1$ strongly, with $r$ depending only on $\varepsilon$; approximation paving instead norm-paves a strongly close bounded perturbation of $x$. Popa and Vaes proved these for type I algebras, amenable Cartan inclusions and profinite actions with $O(\varepsilon^{-4})$ bounds, and quadratic bounds for singular MASAs in ultraproducts. Conjecture 2.8: is every MASA in every von Neumann algebra so-pavable and approximation-pavable, and can so-paving always be achieved with $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ projections?

fields.name: The limiting free energy of orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses at every temperature
fields.shortName: Pressure of orthogonally invariant spin glasses
fields.field: Spin glasses: mean-field models with rotationally invariant couplings
fields.statement: Let $\Lambda_N$ be real diagonal matrices whose empirical spectral laws converge to a compactly supported $\mu$, $U_N$ Haar on $O(N)$, and $P_N=N^{-1}\log\big(2^{-N}\sum_{\sigma\in\{\pm1\}^N}\exp\{\tfrac12\sigma^TU_N^T\Lambda_NU_N\sigma\}\big)$. This family includes the random orthogonal model and Gaussian Hopfield interactions; Marinari, Parisi and Ritort (1994) and Cherrier, Dean and Lefevre (2003) gave replica-symmetric and one-step replica-symmetry-breaking predictions for its free energy in terms of the spectral law. Rigorous results covered only high temperature: Bhattacharya-Sen (zero field), Fan-Wu (external field), Fan-Misiakiewicz-Wang-Wen. Fan and Wu note that for these models replica predictions for the free energy are conjectured but not rigorously known. Does $P_N$ converge at every temperature, and to what variational formula in terms of $\mu$?

fields.name: Must a reflexive Banach space with no AUC renorming contain the countably branching diamonds uniformly? (Baudier-Lancien Problem 39)
fields.field: Banach space theory: asymptotic geometry and metric embeddings
fields.statement: A norm is asymptotically uniformly convex (AUC) if $\overline\delta(t)=\inf_{\|x\|=1}\sup_{F}\inf_{y\in F,\|y\|=1}(\|x+ty\|-1)>0$ for all $t>0$, $F$ ranging over finite-codimensional subspaces, and asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex (AMUC) if the same holds for the average of $\|x+ty\|$ and $\|x-ty\|$. The countably branching diamonds $D_k$ replace each edge by countably many two-edge paths, $k$ times. Baudier, Causey, Dilworth, Kutzarova, Randrianarivony, Schlumprecht and Zhang (2017) proved that an equivalent AMUC norm prevents uniform bi-Lipschitz embeddings of the $D_k$, and that for reflexive spaces with unconditional asymptotic structure, failure of AUC renormability forces uniform diamond embeddings; Swift and Perreau extended the latter under similar structure. Baudier and Lancien record the general question as Problem 39: if $X$ is reflexive and admits no equivalent AUC norm, must the countably branching diamonds embed into $X$ with uniformly bounded distortion?
fields.posedBy: F. P. Baudier and G. Lancien, Asymptotic and nonlinear geometries of Banach spaces and their interactions (arXiv 2512.00817, 2025; Cours Specialises 33, SMF 2026), Problem 39
fields.ageNote: The year is the arXiv posting of the monograph that numbers the problem; the question grows out of Baudier et al. (2017), who proved the implication under unconditional asymptotic structure. Whether that 2017 paper already stated it as open was not checked here.

The Lean statement covers the headline: the full dual of the specified segment-norm space is infinite-dimensional, separable and reflexive, no equivalent norm is AUC, the averaged midpoint modulus is at least $\sqrt{1+t^2/12}-1$, and every embedding of the depth-$k$ diamond has distortion at least $\sqrt{1+k/12}$. That is exactly a reflexive non-AUC-renormable space without uniform diamond embeddings. The six companions give further AMUC non-AUC examples, each with its own Comparator statement.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: the dual $X=J^*$ of a countably branching segment-forest space with finite, unbounded component heights is infinite-dimensional, separable and reflexive, admits no equivalent AUC norm, and its given norm has averaged midpoint modulus $\widehat\delta_X(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/12}-1$; every embedding of $D_k$ into $X$ has distortion at least $\sqrt{1+k/12}$. So Problem 39 has a negative answer, and AMUC does not imply AUC renormability even for reflexive spaces (Baudier had shown the non-reflexive separation in 2026). fields.name: The classification of closed Einstein four-manifolds with positive sectional curvature
fields.field: Riemannian geometry; Einstein metrics in dimension four
fields.statement: A Riemannian metric is Einstein if $\mathrm{Ric}=\lambda g$. The round $S^4$, the round $\mathbb{RP}^4$ and the Fubini-Study $\mathbb{CP}^2$ are closed Einstein four-manifolds with strictly positive sectional curvature. Yang (2000, Conjecture 1) conjectured that these are the only ones. Earlier results needed extra hypotheses: Berger's strict quarter pinching (1961), quantitative pinching bounds of Yang, Costa and Cao-Tran, Gursky-LeBrun's nonzero positive-definite intersection form, and in 2026 topological conditions of Cheng ($\chi\le3$) and Gursky-Malchiodi ($2\chi-3|\tau|\le4$). Is every connected closed Einstein four-manifold with $K>0$, after positive rescaling, isometric to round $S^4$, round $\mathbb{RP}^4$ or Fubini-Study $\mathbb{CP}^2$?
fields.posedBy: DaGang Yang, Rigidity of Einstein 4-manifolds with positive curvature (Invent. Math., 2000), Conjecture 1
fields.ageNote: The year is that of Yang's explicit statement, which the manuscript cites. The question is older in spirit: Berger's 1961 quarter-pinching rigidity is the first partial answer the manuscript lists.

The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family has three manuscripts: the strictly positive classification (September 23, 2026), a zero-plane rigidity theorem extending it to nonnegative curvature (October 4) and an L2 topological gap that uses that classification as a stated premise (October 5). The principal manuscript ships an exact-arithmetic verifier for its finite polynomial sign certificates; its coverage note says it checks only those finite claims, not the geometric or analytic reductions.

fields.name: The dimension exponent of first-order query complexity for well-conditioned log-concave sampling
fields.field: Sampling algorithms; oracle complexity
fields.statement:
Let $V\in C^2(\mathbb R^d)$ with $V(0)=0$, $
abla V(0)=0$ and $I_d\preceq
abla^2V\preceq2I_d$, and let $\pi_V\propto e^{-V}$. An algorithm queries $(V(x),
abla V(x))$ adaptively and must output a sample within total variation $\varepsilon$ of $\pi_V$. Chewi's book Log-Concave Sampling calls it a fundamental open question to determine, up to a universal constant, the minimum number of first-order queries needed uniformly over this class. Known upper bounds grew polynomially in $d$ (about $d^{1/2}$ for Langevin-type methods, $\widetilde O(d^{1/3})$, then $\widetilde O(d^{1/6})$ expected queries), and the lower bounds of Chewi et al. were logarithmic. What is the query complexity, and in particular, is a positive power of $d$ necessary at fixed accuracy?
fields.posedBy: Sinho Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling (book draft), preface: 'a fundamental open question about the complexity of log-concave sampling'
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites no posing source. The statement was read in the preface of the current draft of Chewi's book (version dated August 20, 2026); the year the question first appeared in the draft was not established here, so yearPosed is left null. Chewi, de Dios Pont, Li, Lu and Narayanan (2023) proved the first dimension-dependent lower bounds for this class.

This family is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family is a single manuscript dated September 26, 2026.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the abstract, introduction and Theorem 1.1 were read against the question as stated in Chewi's book. The book asks for the complexity up to a universal constant at accuracy $\varepsilon$; the paper fixes TV accuracy 1/10 and determines only the dimension exponent, so this entry is partial. Lean: formalization.yaml lists ComparatorChallenges/LogConcaveQuery.json with declaration OAI.LogConcaveSampling.exact_source_main in OAI/Probability/LogConcave/Main.lean. The challenge statement was read: for admissible potentials (C2, V(0)=0, gradient zero at 0, Hessian between I and 2I), measurable randomized adaptive algorithms with a deterministic query budget, TV at most 1/10, it asserts queryComplexity(d) <= C d^eps for every eps>0, >= c log d eventually, and gammaStar = 0. That is the headline claim. Not rebuilt here. The paper states that computation between queries is unrestricted and no arithmetic or bit cost is bounded.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: in the exact first-order oracle model with unrestricted computation between queries, for every $\varepsilon>0$ the worst-case query budget $Q(d)$ for TV error $1/10$ satisfies $Q(d)\le C_\varepsilon d^{\varepsilon}$ for all $d\ge2$, on every execution; and $Q(d)\ge c\log d$ for arbitrary randomized adaptive algorithms. Hence the optimal dimension exponent is $\gamma_*=0$. Not shown: the growth rate of $Q(d)$ beyond the exponent (no polylogarithmic bound is claimed), dependence on the accuracy or condition number, or any running-time bound; the constants and approximation orders depend on $\varepsilon$.

fields.significanceNote: The question is central to the theory of sampling algorithms but specialist; the result settles the dimension exponent, not the full complexity the question asks for. fields.field: Complex algebraic geometry; Kahler geometry
fields.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth connected complex projective variety whose anticanonical bundle $-K_X$ carries a smooth Hermitian metric of semipositive curvature (equivalently, by Yau's theorem, a Kahler metric of nonnegative Ricci curvature in that class). Such $-K_X$ is nef. Demailly-Peternell-Schneider and Campana-Demailly-Peternell described the universal cover of such $X$, but the existence of anticanonical sections was open in general; for nef log-anticanonical divisors it was known only in dimension three and under fiber semiampleness. The manuscript attaches the question to Yau's Problem 75. Does $H^0(X,-mK_X)\ne0$ for some integer $m>0$?

fields.name: Kirchberg's embedding problem: does every separable C*-algebra embed in a norm ultrapower of the Cuntz algebra O2?
fields.field: Operator algebras; model theory of C*-algebras
fields.statement: Kirchberg and Phillips proved that every separable unital exact C*-algebra embeds unitally into the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal O_2$. Kirchberg asked how far this universality extends beyond exact algebras once $\mathcal O_2$ is replaced by its norm ultrapower $\mathcal O_2^\omega$. Goldbring and Sinclair (2015) named this Kirchberg's embedding problem and showed its equivalence with existential closedness statements; it is distinct from Connes' embedding problem and from the tensor-norm form of Kirchberg's QWEP conjecture. Does every separable unital C*-algebra admit a unital embedding into $\mathcal O_2^\omega$ for a free ultrafilter $\omega$ on $\mathbb N$?

fields.name: Conformal universality of bulk spin and energy correlations for weakly interacting square-lattice Ising models

fields.name: The Lee-Uhlmann conjecture: smooth anisotropic Calderon uniqueness in dimension at least three, from one boundary patch
fields.field: Inverse problems; elliptic PDE on manifolds
fields.statement: Let $(M,g)$ be a compact connected smooth Riemannian manifold with boundary, $n=\dim M\ge3$, and $\Lambda_g$ its Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for $\Delta_g$. Diffeomorphisms fixing the boundary preserve $\Lambda_g$. Calderon (1980) posed the conductivity problem; Lee and Uhlmann (1989) proved that $\Lambda_g$ determines $g$ up to such a diffeomorphism for real-analytic metrics, and the smooth case became the anisotropic Calderon problem, solved before only for analytic or Einstein metrics, near special backgrounds, or on conformally transversally anisotropic manifolds. The partial-data version, with input and output on the same open boundary patch, was open even for smooth scalar conductivities. For smooth metrics and $n\ge3$, does $\Lambda_g$ (or its restriction to one boundary patch) determine $g$ up to a diffeomorphism fixing the measured boundary?

fields.name: Calderon's uniqueness question for bounded measurable scalar conductivities in dimension three
fields.field: Inverse problems; elliptic PDE

fields.name: Franz-Parisi jamming exponents in the negative spherical perceptron, at margin -1
fields.field: Spin glasses; jamming; random constraint satisfaction
fields.statement: In the spherical perceptron with negative margin, $x\in\sqrt N S^{N-1}$ must satisfy $g^a\cdot x/\sqrt N\ge\sigma$ for $M=\alpha N$ Gaussian patterns, and the feasible set is nonconvex. Rigorous work gave only density bounds. Does the negative perceptron have a sharp jamming threshold with these gap and force exponents?

fields.name: The finite-temperature free energy of the spherical perceptron with bounded continuous potentials (Gyorgyi-Reimann continuous-RSB formula)
fields.field: Spin glasses; perceptron models
fields.statement: For $x$ uniform on the sphere of radius $\sqrt N$ in $\mathbb R^N$, $M=\lfloor\alpha N\rfloor$ standard Gaussian patterns and a single-pattern potential $\phi$, the pressure is $p_N=N^{-1}\log\int e^{\beta\sum_a\phi(g^a\cdot x/\sqrt N)}d\sigma_N(x)$. Gyorgyi and Reimann (2000) derived a continuous replica-symmetry-breaking formula for the finite-temperature model, which in general is not replica-symmetric and not a Gaussian spin glass. fields.name: The polynomial removal conjecture for ordered binary matrices
fields.field: Extremal combinatorics; property testing
fields.statement: For a fixed binary $k\times k$ matrix $H$, an ordered copy in a binary $n\times n$ matrix $A$ is a choice of rows $r_1<\dots<r_k$ and columns $c_1<\dots<c_k$ with $A(r_i,c_j)=H(i,j)$, zeros included. Alon, Ben-Eliezer and Fischer proved qualitative ordered removal: if $A$ is $\epsilon$-far from $H$-free (at least $\epsilon n^2$ entry changes needed), it has at least $\delta(\epsilon)n^{2k}$ copies. Alon and Ben-Eliezer (Problem 1.4) asked whether $\delta$ can be polynomial, and Gishboliner and Shapira conjectured it for each single $H$. Are there $c_H,C_H>0$ with $N_H(A)\ge c_H\epsilon^{C_H}n^{2k}$ whenever $A$ is $\epsilon$-far from $H$-free?

fields.name: Chen's conjecture on smooth long-time existence of the Calabi flow
fields.shortName: Chen's Calabi flow long-time existence conjecture
fields.field: Kahler geometry, geometric flows
fields.statement: Calabi introduced the Calabi flow $\partial_t\phi=S(\omega_\phi)-\bar S$, $\omega_\phi=\omega_0+i\partial\bar\partial\phi$, to search for extremal and constant-scalar-curvature Kahler metrics in a fixed Kahler class of a compact Kahler manifold. Short-time existence and stability near cscK metrics were proved by Chen and He, and global existence is known on Riemann surfaces. Chen conjectured that the flow exists smoothly for all positive time from arbitrary smooth Kahler initial data (He-Zeng 2021, Conjecture 1.1); Chen and Cheng emphasized the case of classes containing a cscK metric. Does the smooth Calabi flow starting from any smooth Kahler metric on a compact Kahler manifold exist for all time?
fields.posedBy: Xiuxiong Chen
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites the conjecture as stated in He and Zeng, The Calabi flow with rough initial data, IMRN 2021, Conjecture 1.1, and Chen-Cheng, JAMS 34 (2021); it does not give the year Chen first stated it, so yearPosed is left blank.

fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a smooth $U(10)$-invariant Kahler form $\omega_0$ on $\mathbb{CP}^{10}$ in the Fubini-Study class whose maximal smooth Calabi flow exists only on $[0,T_*)$ with $0<T_*<\infty$, and at a point $p$ the scalar curvature blows up like $a(T_*-t)^{-1/2}$. Since the class contains the cscK Fubini-Study metric, smooth global existence fails even there. Corollary 1.2 gives finite-time singularities in every complex dimension $n\ge10$ on $\mathbb{CP}^{10}\times\mathbb{CP}^{n-10}$. Not shown: anything in complex dimensions 2 to 9, or about weak (Streets, Berman-Darvas-Lu) flows, which continue to exist.

fields.name: Erdos Problem #138: do the van der Waerden numbers grow superexponentially, W(k)^(1/k) -> infinity?
fields.field: Ramsey theory, arithmetic progressions
fields.statement: Let $W(k)$ be the least $N$ such that every two-colouring of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ contains a monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progression. Classical lower bounds are exponential: Berlekamp gave $W(p+1)>p2^p$ for primes $p$, and the local lemma gives roughly $2^k/k$. Erdos asked whether the growth is in fact superexponential: is it true that $W(k)^{1/k}\to\infty$?

fields.ageNote: Erdos, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory, Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), p. 90, item (2), as cited by the manuscript. Recorded as Erdos Problem 138, whose companion question $W(k+1)-W(k)\to\infty$ is already in the catalog.

fields.name: Bang's half-area cylinder covering question (and the 1-codimensional cylinder covering conjecture)
fields.field: Convex geometry, covering problems
fields.statement: A cylinder in $\mathbb R^3$ is $B+\mathbb Ru$ with $u$ a unit vector and $B\subset u^\perp$ of finite area. Bang's plank theorem says plank widths in a covering of a convex body sum to at least its minimal width; for cylinders, the two-cylinder cover of a regular tetrahedron has total base area exactly half the minimum projection area $A_{\min}(K)$. Bezdek and Litvak, attributing the example to Bang (1951), asked whether every finite cylinder covering of a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ satisfies $\sum_i|B_i|\ge\frac12A_{\min}(K)$; Bezdek and Khan conjectured the stronger directionwise bound $\sum_i|B_i|/|\pi_{u_i^\perp}K|\ge\frac12$. Do these half-area lower bounds hold?
fields.posedBy: Thoger Bang (example); Karoly Bezdek and Alexander Litvak; Karoly Bezdek and Muhammad Khan (directionwise form)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Bezdek (2009, Problem 3.1) and Bezdek-Litvak (2009), who attribute the tetrahedral example and the half-area question to Bang's 1951 plank paper; the directionwise form is Bezdek-Khan (arXiv 1602.06040, 2016), Conjecture 4.13. Bezdek-Litvak proved the directionwise bound 1/3 in general.

fields.name: Siegel-Yao Conjecture A: symplectic packings of balls into a ball in dimension at least six
fields.field: Symplectic geometry, embedding problems
fields.statement: Let $B^{2n}(R)$ be the closed ball of capacity $R$ (capacity $\pi$ times squared radius) in $(\mathbb C^n,\omega_0)$. Two obstructions to embedding $\bigsqcup_iB^{2n}(R_i)$ symplectically into the interior of $B^{2n}(R)$ are known: volume, $\sum_iR_i^n<R^n$, and Gromov's two-ball obstruction, $R_i+R_j<R$. In dimension four further obstructions exist. Siegel and Yao conjectured (Conjecture A) that in dimension $2n\ge6$ these two are the only ones. For $n\ge3$, is every finite family of closed balls satisfying both inequalities symplectically embeddable into the open ball?
fields.posedBy: Kyler Siegel and Yuan Yao

fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for $n\ge3$, $k\ge1$ and positive $R,R_1,\dots,R_k$, the closed balls $B^{2n}(R_i)$ embed disjointly and symplectically into $\mathrm{Int}\,B^{2n}(R)$ if and only if $\sum_iR_i^n<R^n$ and $R_i+R_j<R$ for $i\ne j$. fields.name: Cardy's formula for critical Poisson-Voronoi percolation (annealed crossing part of Schramm's Problem 2.12)
fields.field: Percolation, conformal invariance
fields.statement: In critical planar Voronoi percolation, the cells of a Poisson point process of intensity $\varepsilon^{-2}$ are coloured black or white independently with probability $1/2$. Cardy predicted, and Smirnov proved for site percolation on the triangular lattice, that crossing probabilities of a conformal quadrilateral converge to Cardy's hypergeometric function of its conformal modulus. Schramm (ICM 2006, Problem 2.12) asked for the corresponding conformal-invariance theorem for Voronoi percolation. Do the crossing probabilities of critical Poisson-Voronoi percolation in a Jordan quadrilateral converge to Cardy's formula, and is the scaling limit conformally invariant?
fields.posedBy: Oded Schramm
fields.ageNote: Schramm, Proceedings of the ICM 2006 (Madrid), Problem 2.12, as cited by the manuscript; Benjamini and Schramm had earlier studied conformal invariance of Voronoi percolation (1998).
fields.aiRole: The release README says every result in it was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model following a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The principal manuscript (September 23, 2026) proves the annealed Cardy formula; two companions (October 5, 2026) take it as an input to prove a pivotal-count asymptotic and quenched near-critical universality of crossing thresholds.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the introduction and Theorem 1.1 were read against Schramm's Problem 2.12 as the manuscript cites it. Both companions are conditional on the principal paper's theorem. No Lean formalization accompanies this family. Uses established box-crossing and quenched-annealed comparison inputs (Tassion, Ahlberg-Griffiths-Morris-Tassion, Vanneuville).
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every bounded Jordan domain with four marked boundary points, the annealed probability of a black crossing in critical Poisson-Voronoi percolation converges to Cardy's function $F(x)$ of the conformal cross-ratio $x$. A corollary gives a quenched $L^2$ limit for fixed rectangles. The companions prove that the expected number of pivotal cells for a unit-square crossing is asymptotic to $c\,\varepsilon^{-3/4}$ and that conditional near-critical crossing-threshold laws for rational polygonal quads converge in probability over tessellations to the triangular-lattice law. Not shown: convergence of interfaces to SLE(6) or the full conformal invariance of Schramm's problem.

fields.name: The Bogomolov-Pop conjecture: function fields over algebraically closed fields are determined by their pro-l abelian-by-central Galois groups
fields.field: Birational anabelian geometry
fields.statement: Let $K/k$ be a function field of transcendence degree at least two over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic different from a prime $\ell$, and let $\Pi_K^c$ be the maximal pro-$\ell$ quotient of its absolute Galois group in which commutators are central, with abelianization $\Pi_K^a$. Bogomolov (1991) proposed that this small quotient determines the field; the precise Isom form, with its scalar and Frobenius ambiguities, is Conjecture 1 in Topaz (2016). Known cases had constants an algebraic closure of a finite field (Bogomolov-Tschinkel, Pop) or extra inertia data (Pop). Is the natural map from field isomorphisms of perfect closures, modulo Frobenius, to bracket-compatible isomorphisms $\Pi_L^a\to\Pi_K^a$ modulo $\mathbb Z_\ell^\times$ a bijection?
fields.posedBy: Fedor Bogomolov; Isom form recorded by Adam Topaz
fields.ageNote: Bogomolov, On two conjectures in birational algebraic geometry (1991), as cited by the manuscript; the precise Isom formulation is Topaz, Reconstructing function fields from rational quotients of mod-l Galois groups, Math. Ann. 366 (2016), Introduction, Conjecture 1.

fields.name: Is the free uniform spanning forest a factor of IID?
fields.shortName: FUSF as a factor of IID
fields.field: Probability on graphs, uniform spanning forests
fields.statement: The free uniform spanning forest (FUSF) of an infinite connected locally finite graph is the weak limit of uniform spanning trees on finite exhaustions, without wiring the boundary. The wired forest is a factor of IID on transient graphs via Wilson's algorithm rooted at infinity, and Timar proved the free forest is a factor of IID on recurrent and invariantly amenable unimodular random graphs. Lyons (2013) asked, for Cayley graphs, whether the FUSF is a factor of IID. Can the FUSF be generated as an equivariant measurable factor of independent vertex labels, in general and in particular on nonamenable Cayley graphs?

fields.ageNote: Lyons, l2-Betti numbers, cost, and the free uniform spanning forest, Oberwolfach Reports 10 (2013), p. 2392, as cited by the manuscript; Timar (arXiv, December 2025 version) states the unrestricted question as open.

fields.name: Fast mixing of Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model throughout the high-temperature phase, zero external field
fields.shortName: SK Glauber dynamics spectral gap for all beta < 1
fields.field: Spin glasses, Markov chain mixing
fields.statement: For the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model with couplings $J_{ij}\sim N(0,\beta^2/n)$, single-site Glauber (heat-bath) dynamics resamples one spin from its conditional Gibbs law. Open Problem 15 of the ETH randomstrasse101 list asks: considering the SK model with an arbitrary external field, does Glauber dynamics fast mix (in polynomial time) up to the replica symmetry breaking threshold $\beta^*=1$?

fields.name: The Kuhn-Lloyd question: does the chromatic fixed-point loss of a p-group equal the shortest cyclic subnormal chain length?
fields.field: Equivariant stable homotopy theory, chromatic homotopy
fields.statement: For a finite $p$-group $G$, a subgroup $H$ and $n\ge0$, let $r_n(G,H)$ be the least $r$ such that $K(n+r)_*(\Phi^HX)=0$ implies $K(n)_*(\Phi^GX)=0$ for every finite $p$-local genuine $G$-spectrum $X$, where $K(i)$ is Morava K-theory. This controls the inclusions among primes in the Balmer spectrum of finite $G$-spectra. Let $\ell(G,H)$ be the shortest length of a subnormal chain from $H$ to $G$ with cyclic quotients; then $r_n\le\ell$. The abelian case was settled by Barthel et al., and Kuhn and Lloyd proved equality for central extensions of elementary abelian 2-groups by $C_2$. They expressed hope that $r_n(G,H)=\ell(G,H)$ in general and asked whether the loss is independent of the height $n$. Is $r_n(G,H)=\ell(G,H)$ for all finite $p$-groups?
fields.posedBy: Nicholas J. Kuhn and Christopher J. R. Lloyd
fields.ageNote: Kuhn-Lloyd, Amer. J. Math. 146 (2024), 769-812, Section 2.2, as cited by the manuscript; phrased as a 'cautious hope' plus an explicit question on height independence, not a formal conjecture.

fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every prime $p$, finite $p$-group $G$, subgroup $H$ and $n\ge0$, $r_n(G,H)=\ell(G,H)$, the shortest cyclic subnormal chain length; sharpness is witnessed by finite spectra, and the case $n=0$ includes rational detection. fields.name: Uniqueness of DiPerna-Lions renormalized solutions of the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
fields.field: Kinetic theory; Boltzmann equation, weak solutions
fields.statement: DiPerna and Lions (1989) proved global existence and weak stability of renormalized solutions of the inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation $(\partial_t+v\cdot\nabla_x)F=Q(F,F)$ for any nonnegative initial density with finite mass, energy and entropy, $\int F_0(1+|v|^2+|\log F_0|)<\infty$; these bounds alone do not make the collision term locally integrable. Uniqueness is known only under much stronger control (Maxwellian upper bounds, perturbations of a Maxwellian in weighted Sobolev spaces), and for the spatially homogeneous hard-sphere equation. The uniqueness problem for general renormalized solutions is listed as open, for example in Silvestre's 2022 survey of open problems in kinetic equations, and Gismondi, Golding and Novack (2026) conjectured nonuniqueness. For the hard-sphere kernel on $\mathbb T^3\times\mathbb R^3$, are renormalized (entropy) solutions with finite mass, energy and entropy determined uniquely by their initial datum?

fields.name: The cotype-cotype conjecture: finite cotype of a Banach space and its dual implies K-convexity (approximation property case)
fields.field: Banach space geometry; Rademacher type and cotype, K-convexity
fields.statement: A Banach space $X$ is $K$-convex if the Rademacher projections on $L_2(\{-1,1\}^s;X)$ are uniformly bounded; by Maurey-Pisier and Pisier this is equivalent to nontrivial Rademacher type. If $X$ is $K$-convex then $X$ and $X^*$ have finite cotype. Pisier (1980-81) proved the converse when $X$ has the bounded approximation property and the cotype exponents $q,r$ of $X,X^*$ satisfy a restriction, and asked whether the restriction can be removed (Remark 2(iii)). Without any approximation hypothesis the converse fails (Pisier 1983). Szarek and Tomczak-Jaegermann (2009) call this the cotype-cotype conjecture, and Gupta, Misra and Ray (2025, Conjecture 1.5) state the BAP form. If $X$ has the (bounded) approximation property and both $X$ and $X^*$ have finite cotype, with arbitrary exponents, must $X$ be $K$-convex?
fields.posedBy: G. Pisier, Seminaire d'analyse fonctionnelle 1980-81, expose VII, Remark 2(iii); named the cotype-cotype conjecture by Szarek and Tomczak-Jaegermann (2009)

The family is in lean/formalization.yaml (ComparatorChallenges/Cotype.json, declaration OAI.Cotype.mainTarget_proved, file OAI/Analysis/Cotype/Main.lean). The comparator statement was read here: for every nontrivial real Banach space with the approximation property, K-convexity (uniform bound on finite-cube Rademacher projections) is equivalent to finite cotype of $X$ and of its continuous dual. This is the headline claim. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: a nonzero real Banach space $X$ with the approximation property is $K$-convex if and only if $C_q(X)<\infty$ and $C_r(X^*)<\infty$ for some $q,r\in[2,\infty)$, possibly different; equivalently such $X$ has nontrivial Rademacher type. Corollary 1.2 makes the bound on $K(X)$ uniform in the cotype data and gives dimension-free metric-entropy duality for the corresponding convex bodies; a further consequence settles a Gupta-Misra-Ray tensor-norm conjecture (their Conjecture 1.4) under AP. Real scalars only; constants are existential. It does not address spaces failing AP, where the statement is false.

fields.name: Constant-competitive single-sample prophet inequalities on general matroids
fields.field: Online algorithms; prophet inequalities and matroid secretary problems
fields.statement: In a matroid prophet inequality, independent nonnegative values $V_e$ on the elements of a known matroid $M$ arrive one at a time and an online rule must irrevocably accept or reject each, keeping the accepted set independent; it is compared with $\mathbb E[\mathrm{OPT}_M(V)]$. With known distributions, Kleinberg and Weinberg (2012) achieve 1/2. Azar, Kleinberg and Weinberg (2014) introduced the limited-information model in which the rule only gets one independent sample from each unknown distribution, and related it to order-oblivious matroid secretary algorithms. For general matroids only a doubly logarithmic loss in the rank was known with one sample (Feldman-Svensson-Zenklusen), and constant guarantees needed polylogarithmically many samples (Fu et al. 2024). Is there a single-sample rule achieving a constant fraction of the expected offline optimum on every matroid?
fields.posedBy: Azar, Kleinberg and Weinberg (SODA 2014) introduced single-sample prophet inequalities; Fu, Lu, Tang, Wu, Wu and Zhang (EC 2024) describe the general-matroid single-sample question as open
fields.ageNote: The manuscript does not quote an explicit statement of the question. 2014 is the Azar-Kleinberg-Weinberg framework it cites; the abstract of Fu et al. fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a measurable online rule, independent of the value laws, which for every finite matroid and every independent family of samples $S_e$ and values $V_e$ with common laws and $\mathbb E[\mathrm{OPT}_M(V)]<\infty$ accepts an independent set with expected value at least $2^{-310}\mathbb E[\mathrm{OPT}_M(V)]$, against an adversary that chooses the order after seeing samples, values and the full random seed (the proof gives $2^{-293}$). fields.name: The Solomon-Yau least-volume conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces of round spheres
fields.field: Minimal hypersurfaces in spheres; volume gaps
fields.statement: The equator is the least-volume closed minimal hypersurface of the unit sphere $S^{m+1}$. The minimal Clifford products $S^k(\sqrt{k/m})\times S^{m-k}(\sqrt{(m-k)/m})$, $1\le k<m$, are the natural next examples; let $a_m$ be the least of their volumes. Cheng, Li and Yau (1984) proved a dimension-dependent volume gap above the equator, and for $m=2$ the sharp bound $2\pi^2$ follows from the Marques-Neves proof of the Willmore conjecture. Yau's problem list (Problem 31) asks for the next volume level, and Ge and Li (2021, Conjecture 1.12(ii)) state it as the Solomon-Yau conjecture. For every $m\ge2$, does every closed minimal hypersurface of $S^{m+1}$ that is not totally geodesic have volume at least $a_m$?
fields.posedBy: S.-T. Yau, Open problems in geometry (1994), Problem 31; formulated as the Solomon-Yau conjecture by J. Ge and F. Li (2021, Conjecture 1.12(ii))
fields.ageNote: 1994 is the year of the Yau problem list as cited by the manuscript; the name credits B. Solomon as well, without a separate citation in the manuscript.

fields.name: Schramm's Hausdorff-measure problem for SLE: an exact gauge function for the chordal SLE trace, 0 < kappa < 8
fields.field: Schramm-Loewner evolution; fractal geometry of random curves
fields.statement: For $0<\kappa<8$ the chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ trace has Hausdorff dimension $d=1+\kappa/8$ (Beffara 2008), and Rezaei (2018) proved its $d$-dimensional Hausdorff measure is zero. For a gauge $h$ (continuous, nondecreasing, $h(0)=0$) let $\mathcal H^h$ be the corresponding Hausdorff measure. Schramm, in his 2006 ICM collection of problems (Problem 7.1), asked whether the SLE trace has a sigma-finite Hausdorff measure and suggested $r^d\log\log(1/r)$ as a possible gauge. Is there a deterministic gauge $h$ such that almost surely $0<\mathcal H^h(\gamma([s,t]))<\infty$ for nontrivial trace segments, and if so, which?

fields.name: Erdos Problem #371: do the integers with P(n) < P(n+1) have density 1/2? (Erdos-Pomerance joint independence of largest prime factors)
fields.field: Analytic number theory; smooth numbers and largest prime factors
fields.statement: Let $P^+(n)$ be the largest prime factor of $n$ and $\rho$ the Dickman function, so that $P^+(n)\le n^a$ has density $\rho(1/a)$. Erdos and Pomerance (1978) conjectured that the largest prime factors of $n$ and $n+1$ behave independently, so that $P^+(n)\le n^a$ and $P^+(n+1)\le n^b$ hold simultaneously with density $\rho(1/a)\rho(1/b)$, and in particular that the set of $n$ with $P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)$ has natural density $1/2$ (Erdos Problem #371). They proved positive lower density for each ordering; later bounds reached about $0.28$. Teravainen (2018) proved the logarithmic-density version and Tao and Teravainen (2019) the natural-density version at almost all scales. Does $\{n:P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)\}$ have natural density $1/2$, and are $\log P^+(n)/\log n$ and $\log P^+(n+1)/\log n$ asymptotically independent?

fields.name: The Ara-Maltsiniotis conjecture: Thomason model structures on strict n-categories for every n
fields.field: Homotopy theory; strict higher categories and model structures
fields.statement: Thomason (1980) put a model structure on small categories, transferred from simplicial sets along $c_1\mathrm{Sd}^2\dashv\mathrm{Ex}^2N_1$, that is Quillen equivalent to simplicial sets. For strict globular $n$-categories, $1\le n\le\infty$, with the Street nerve $N_n$ built from orientals, Ara and Maltsiniotis (2014) proved the case $n=2$, reduced the general case to two conditions, and conjectured the general statement; Ara (2023) and Guetta-Maltsiniotis (2024) restate it. Is there, for every $n$ including $\omega$, a model structure on small strict $n$-categories whose weak equivalences and fibrations are those maps sent by $\mathrm{Ex}^2N_n$ to weak equivalences and Kan fibrations, and is $c_n\mathrm{Sd}^2\dashv\mathrm{Ex}^2N_n$ a Quillen equivalence with simplicial sets?
fields.posedBy: D. Ara and G. Maltsiniotis, Vers une structure de categorie de modeles a la Thomason sur la categorie des n-categories strictes, Adv. Math. 259 (2014)

That is the headline. The challenge file is about 136 KB because it defines strict omega-categories and orientals itself; those definitions were not audited. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $n\in\{1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$, the classes $W_n=N_n^{-1}(W_{KQ})$, $F_n=(\mathrm{Ex}^2N_n)^{-1}(\mathrm{Fib}_{KQ})$ and $C_n={}^{\perp}(F_n\cap W_n)$ form a proper combinatorial model structure on small strict $n$-categories, cofibrantly generated by the images of boundary and horn inclusions under $c_n\mathrm{Sd}^2$, and $c_n\mathrm{Sd}^2\dashv\mathrm{Ex}^2N_n$ is a Quillen equivalence with Kan-Quillen simplicial sets. The key step proves the Ara-Maltsiniotis pushout condition (Scholie 5.14 (d')). It concerns strict globular categories only, not weak higher categories or n-fold categories.

fields.name: The Nam-Sly-Zhang conjecture: the free Ising state on the d-regular tree is a factor of IID up to the reconstruction threshold
fields.shortName: Free Ising on trees as a factor of IID
fields.field: Ergodic theory on trees; Ising model, factors of IID
fields.statement: Let $T_d$ be the infinite $d$-regular tree, $d\ge3$, and $\mu_{d,\beta}$ the free zero-field ferromagnetic Ising measure with $\theta=\tanh\beta$. A spin law is a factor of IID if it is the law of $\Phi(U)$ for IID uniform vertex labels $U$ and a measurable $\Phi$ commuting with tree automorphisms. Lyons (2017) studied which such Gibbs measures are factors of IID: the free state is one when $\theta\le1/(d-1)$, and Sly's argument shows it is not when $\theta>(d-1)^{-1/2}$, beyond the reconstruction threshold. Nam, Sly and Zhang (arXiv 2020, CMP 2022) proved it is a factor for $\theta\le c/\sqrt{d-1}$ and $d\ge d_0$ and conjectured the sharp threshold. Is $\mu_{d,\beta}$ a factor of IID for every $d\ge3$ whenever $\tanh\beta\le(d-1)^{-1/2}$, including equality?
fields.posedBy: D. Nam, A. Sly and L. Zhang, Ising model on trees and factors of IID (arXiv 2012.09484, 2020; Comm. Math. Phys. 2022), following R. Lyons, Factors of IID on trees (2017)
fields.ageNote: The Nam-Sly-Zhang preprint appeared in December 2020 and was published in 2022; Lyons's broader question on factor-of-IID Gibbs measures on trees dates from arXiv 2014, published 2017.

fields.name: Robert's trace-cone question: does the cone of extended traces classify W-stabilized separable nuclear C*-algebras?
fields.field: Operator algebras; classification of nuclear C*-algebras
fields.statement: The Razak-Jacelon algebra $\mathcal W$ is simple, monotracial, stably projectionless and nuclear; tensoring with it removes K-theory and leaves trace data. For a C*-algebra $A$ let $T(A)$ be the cone of all lower-semicontinuous extended traces $A_+\to[0,\infty]$, including the zero/infinity weights of ideals, with its canonical topology (Elliott-Robert-Santiago). Known classification results cover simple algebras and the traceless (purely infinite) case. Leonel Robert asked, as recorded by Santiago (2012) and listed as Problem LXVIII by Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White, whether this cone is a complete invariant: if $A,B$ are separable nuclear C*-algebras with $T(A)\cong T(B)$ as topological cones, is $A\otimes\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal K\cong B\otimes\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal K$?
fields.posedBy: Leonel Robert, recorded in L. Santiago, W-stable C*-algebras (West Coast Operator Algebra Seminar abstract, 2012); Problem LXVIII in Schafhauser-Tikuisis-White, Nuclear C*-algebras: 99 problems

The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against Robert's question in the Schafhauser-Tikuisis-White formulation, which keeps every extended trace including the ideal weights. The theorem assumes only separability and nuclearity, allows arbitrary ideal structure and both finite and infinite subquotients, and needs no UCT. The release has no Lean formalization for this family (lean/docs/301.md does not exist at the pinned commit). The proof combines existence and uniqueness theorems with an approximate intertwining; it was not refereed here.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if $A,B$ are separable nuclear complex C*-algebras and $T(A)\cong T(B)$ as topological cones, then $A\otimes\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal K\cong B\otimes\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal K$, and the isomorphism can be chosen to induce the given cone map. No density condition on finite domains of the weights and no UCT is assumed. It does not classify algebras without the $\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal K$ stabilization, and does not determine the range of the invariant.

fields.name: Almost-sure global well-posedness for high-regularity random data in energy-supercritical defocusing NLS (Deng-Nahmod-Yue Open Problem 3), refuted on the twelve-torus
fields.shortName: Stable blowup for supercritical defocusing NLS
fields.field: Dispersive PDE; nonlinear Schrodinger equation; random data; blowup
fields.statement: Consider the defocusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation $i\partial_t u+\Delta u=|u|^{p-1}u$ on the torus $\mathbb T^d$ with odd $p$, in the energy-supercritical range $s_{cr}=d/2-2/(p-1)>1$, where the conserved energy does not control the regularity needed for global classical solutions. Deng, Nahmod and Yue (2020) observed that if classical solutions with random initial data of high regularity, such as Gaussian Fourier series $\sum_n g_n\langle n\rangle^{-\alpha}e^{in\cdot x}$ with $\alpha$ large, were almost surely global, then blowup for these equations would be non-generic and unstable, as the known whole-space blowup examples are. Their Open Problem 3 asks: in the energy-supercritical case, does almost-sure global well-posedness hold for random initial data of high regularity?
fields.posedBy: Yu Deng, Andrea R. Nahmod and Haitian Yue, Random tensors, propagation of randomness, and nonlinear dispersive equations (arXiv:2006.09285v1, 2020), Section 9.2.3, Open Problem 3
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Open Problem 3 of Deng-Nahmod-Yue and says its own eventual-alpha, $H^m$ quantified formulation is the one considered there, not a verbatim restatement. The posing text was read here in arXiv v1. The wider question of whether energy-supercritical defocusing NLS can blow up goes back to Bourgain's surveys.

Its statement was read here: stable_blowup gives, for every lower bound, an odd $p\ge3$ above it, an integer $k>8$ and a nonempty open set of Fourier-side $H^k(\mathbb T^{12})$ data whose classical solutions blow up at the self-similar rate $(T-t)^{-1/(p-1)}$ at a point and do not extend continuously past $T$; gaussian_blowup and gaussian_not_almost_sure_global give positive Gaussian probability of that set for every $\alpha>k+6$. fields.resultNote: Claims: there are an odd $p$ (which can be taken arbitrarily large), an integer $k>8$ and a nonempty open set $\mathcal U\subset H^k(\mathbb T^{12})$ such that every solution of the defocusing NLS with data in $\mathcal U$ blows up in finite time $T$ with $(T-t)^{1/(p-1)}|u(t,x_*)|\to c_0>0$, a type-I self-similar singularity with logarithmic phase. Since Gaussian measures charge open sets, for every $\alpha>k+6$ the Gaussian Fourier datum blows up with positive probability, so almost-sure global existence for high-regularity random data fails for this $(d,p)$. It does NOT give probability-one blowup, a bound uniform in $\alpha$, an explicit $p$, or anything for low dimensions such as $d\le 11$; the question for other pairs $(d,p)$ stays open.

fields.name: Naor's question: does nontrivial Markov type force an equivalent uniformly smooth norm (superreflexivity)?
fields.field: Banach space geometry; Ribe program; metric invariants
fields.statement: A normed space $X$ has Markov type $p$ with constant $K$ if for every finite stationary reversible Markov chain $(Z_t)$ on a set $S$, every $f:S\to X$ and every $t\ge1$, $\mathbb E\|f(Z_t)-f(Z_0)\|^p\le K^p\,t\,\mathbb E\|f(Z_1)-f(Z_0)\|^p$. Ball introduced Markov type for Lipschitz extension. Naor, Peres, Schramm and Sheffield showed that uniform smoothness of power type $p$ implies Markov type $p$, so by Pisier's renorming every superreflexive space has Markov type $p$ for some $p>1$. Markov type is a metric property, so a converse would give a metric characterization of superreflexivity in the Ribe program. Naor (2012, Question 4) asked: can a Banach space have nontrivial Markov type (Markov type $p$ for some $p>1$) without admitting an equivalent uniformly smooth norm?
fields.posedBy: Assaf Naor, An introduction to the Ribe program, Japanese Journal of Mathematics 7 (2012), Question 4
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. Its named exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human edited for readability) do not concern this family. The manuscript is credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The main theorem has a Lean formalization listed in the release's formalization catalogue.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. The main theorem was read against Naor's Question 4. formalization.yaml lists ComparatorChallenges/MarkovType.json with declaration OAI.MarkovSuperreflexivity.hasNontrivialMarkovType_iff_hasEquivalentUCNorm in OAI/Analysis/MarkovType/Main.lean. The comparator statement, read here, says that for every real Banach space (CompleteSpace), having Markov type $p$ for some $p>1$, with the inequality required over all finite reversible chains and all times $n\ge1$, is equivalent to admitting an equivalent uniformly convex norm. Given Pisier's duality between uniformly convex and uniformly smooth renormings, which the formal statement does not itself include, this is the headline. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Claims that every real Banach space with Markov type $p$ for at least one $p>1$ admits an equivalent uniformly convex norm, hence is superreflexive and (by Pisier) admits an equivalent uniformly smooth norm. With the known converse (Naor-Peres-Schramm-Sheffield plus Pisier) this characterizes superreflexivity by nontrivial Markov type, answering Naor's question negatively. The proof builds, from a nonreflexive space finitely representable in a non-superreflexive one, a spreading norm and explicit reversible walks whose image has linear displacement. It does NOT address complex scalars separately, the exact Markov type exponent of a given space, or Ball's Markov type 2 questions for specific spaces.
fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Nontrivial Markov Type Forces Superreflexivity
fields.significanceNote: A named question in the Ribe program, which seeks metric characterizations of linear properties of Banach spaces; superreflexivity already had metric characterizations (Bourgain's trees, Mendel-Naor Markov convexity), so this adds a natural one rather than the first. fields.name: Homogeneous depth-five lower bounds for iterated matrix multiplication with unrestricted bottom fan-in (Bera-Chakrabarti question, balanced regime)
fields.field: Algebraic complexity; arithmetic circuit lower bounds
fields.statement: Let $\mathrm{IMM}_{w,d}$ be the $(1,1)$ entry of a product of $d$ generic $w\times w$ matrices. Nisan and Wigderson (1995) asked for superpolynomial lower bounds for homogeneous $\Sigma\Pi\Sigma\Pi\Sigma$ circuits, and Kayal and Saha asked for depth-five bounds for IMM. Bera and Chakrabarti (CCC 2015) proved that homogeneous $\Sigma\Pi\Sigma\Pi\Sigma$ circuits computing $\mathrm{IMM}_{n^q,n}$ in $N$ variables need $N^{\Omega(\sqrt n)}$ gates, but only when every bottom linear form has fan-in at most $N^{\mu}$ with $\mu<1/2$. They called it the most immediate and natural open question whether the bound survives bottom fan-in up to $N^{1-\Theta(1)}$ or $N$, the general case. Does the $\sqrt n$-exponent lower bound for homogeneous depth-five circuits computing IMM hold with unrestricted bottom fan-in?
fields.posedBy: Suman K. Bera and Amit Chakrabarti, A Depth-Five Lower Bound for Iterated Matrix Multiplication (CCC 2015), closing open question; background question of Nisan and Wigderson (1995)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Nisan-Wigderson (1995) and Bera-Chakrabarti (2015) but quotes no posing sentence; the closing sentence of Bera-Chakrabarti was read here. Superpolynomial depth-five lower bounds over characteristic zero already follow from Limaye-Srinivasan-Tavenas (2021), so what remained open was the sharp $\sqrt n$ exponent with unrestricted bottom forms.

fields.name: The isoperimetric conjecture for the cubic flat three-torus (balls, tubes, slabs)
fields.field: Geometric measure theory; periodic isoperimetric problem
fields.statement: In the unit cubic flat torus $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$, which regions of prescribed volume $V$ have least perimeter? The conjecture predicts that the minimizers are, in turn, round balls, solid circular tubes about shortest closed geodesics, and slabs between parallel coordinate tori, followed by their complements, so the profile is $\min\{(36\pi)^{1/3}v^{2/3},2\sqrt{\pi v},2\}$ with $v=\min(V,1-V)$. Small volumes (Morgan-Johnson) and volumes near one half (Acerbi-Fusco-Morini) were known, and Milman reduced the profile to the two transition volumes, but excluding higher-genus competitors in between remained open. Is the ball-tube-slab picture the true isoperimetric profile of the cubic three-torus?

fields.name: The coarse Novikov conjecture for bounded-geometry spaces: is coarse assembly rationally injective?
fields.field: Higher index theory; coarse geometry; operator K-theory
fields.statement: For a uniformly discrete metric space $X$ of bounded geometry, coarse K-homology $KX_*(X)=\varinjlim_r K_*^{lf}(P_r(X))$ is the limit over Rips complexes, and the coarse assembly map $\mu_X:KX_*(X)\to K_*(C^*(X))$ sends a class to its index in the K-theory of the Roe algebra. Roe formulated the coarse index theory and its Novikov-type injectivity question, and Higson and Roe (1995) stated the coarse Baum-Connes conjecture that $\mu_X$ is an isomorphism. Surjectivity was known to fail for some expanders (Higson-Lafforgue-Skandalis), while injectivity was proved under geometric hypotheses such as coarse embeddability in Hilbert space (Yu). The coarse Novikov conjecture asks: is $\mu_X\otimes\mathbb Q$ injective for every bounded-geometry space $X$?
fields.posedBy: John Roe, Coarse cohomology and index theory on complete Riemannian manifolds (Memoirs AMS 497, 1993); Nigel Higson and John Roe, On the coarse Baum-Connes conjecture (1995), Conjecture 6.6
fields.ageNote: The manuscripts credit Roe (1993) with the Novikov-type formulation and Higson-Roe (1995, Conjecture 6.6) with the coarse Baum-Connes conjecture, of which rational injectivity is the Novikov half; no single posing sentence for the bounded-geometry injectivity statement is quoted.

fields.name: Uchida's conjecture on open homomorphisms of Galois groups of solvably closed extensions of number fields
fields.field: Anabelian geometry; Galois groups of number fields
fields.statement: Let $E_i/F_i$ ($i=1,2$) be Galois extensions of number fields with each $E_i$ solvably closed (no nontrivial abelian extension), for example algebraic closures or maximal prosolvable extensions, and write $G_i=\mathrm{Gal}(E_i/F_i)$. The Neukirch-Uchida theorem says that isomorphisms $G_1\cong G_2$ come from field isomorphisms. Uchida (1981) proved the analogous statement for open homomorphisms when the source field is $\mathbb Q$, proved uniqueness in general, and proved existence under a local condition on decomposition groups, and conjectured the general case. Is every continuous homomorphism $\alpha:G_1\to G_2$ with open image induced by a field embedding $j:E_2\hookrightarrow E_1$, i.e. $g\circ j=j\circ\alpha(g)$ for all $g\in G_1$?
fields.posedBy: Koji Uchida, Homomorphisms of Galois groups of solvably closed Galois extensions, J. Math. Soc. Japan 33 (1981), p. 595
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. Its named exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human edited for readability) do not concern this family. The manuscript is credited to OpenAI with no human author named. No Lean formalization of this result is in the release.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. The main theorem was read against Uchida's conjecture as described in the manuscript (Uchida 1981, p. 595); the 1981 paper itself was not opened here. The proof ends by verifying Hoshi's cyclotomic-character criterion (Tohoku 2025), which is an input from the literature, and uses an l-adic Waldschmidt-Masser type statement for which the paper gives its own proof. No Lean formalization exists for this family.
fields.resultNote: Claims Uchida's conjecture in full: for number fields $F_1,F_2$ and possibly infinite solvably closed Galois extensions $E_i/F_i$, every continuous open homomorphism $\mathrm{Gal}(E_1/F_1)\to\mathrm{Gal}(E_2/F_2)$ is induced by a unique field embedding $E_2\hookrightarrow E_1$, with no hypothesis on the kernel and no separate cyclotomic-compatibility assumption. The key steps derive full cyclotomic compatibility from openness, through a uniform (in the auxiliary prime) Kummer bound and Frobenius-average character tests, and then apply Hoshi's criterion. It does NOT treat function fields, finite solvable quotients (Saidi-Tamagawa), or non-open homomorphisms.

fields.name: Bi-Lipschitz charts at every regular point of a noncollapsed RCD(K,n) space
fields.shortName: Bi-Lipschitz charts at RCD regular points
fields.field: Metric measure spaces; synthetic lower Ricci bounds; RCD spaces
fields.statement: Let $(X,d,\mathcal H^n)$ be a noncollapsed $\mathrm{RCD}(K,n)$ space, the synthetic setting containing noncollapsed Ricci limit spaces. A point is regular if every pointed tangent there is $\mathbb R^n$. Mondino-Naber proved bi-Lipschitz rectifiability on measurable pieces and Kapovitch-Mondino gave an open manifold region with bi-Holder charts; Cheeger and Colding (1997) had asked whether bi-Holder parametrizations of quantitatively regular Ricci-limit neighborhoods can be upgraded to bi-Lipschitz. The regular-point conjecture, recalled by Honda and Zhang (2026), asks: does every regular point of a noncollapsed $\mathrm{RCD}(K,n)$ space have an open neighborhood, with the restricted distance, bi-Lipschitz homeomorphic to an open subset of $\mathbb R^n$?
fields.posedBy: Conjecture recalled by Shouhei Honda and Ruobing Zhang (arXiv:2608.16021, 2026), Section 1.2; antecedent question of Jeff Cheeger and Tobias Colding, J. Differential Geom. 46 (1997), Remark 5.15
fields.ageNote: The manuscript says the conjecture is explicitly recalled by Honda and Zhang (2026) and treats Cheeger-Colding (1997, Remark 5.15) as a historical antecedent concerning Ricci-limit neighborhoods; it does not say who first stated the regular-point form or when, so yearPosed is left empty.
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. Its named exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human edited for readability) do not concern this family. The manuscript is credited to OpenAI with no human author named. No Lean formalization of this result is in the release.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Theorem 1.1 was read against the conjecture as the manuscript states it; Honda-Zhang was not opened here. Scope limits the paper states: noncollapsed means the reference measure is exactly $\mathcal H^n$; regularity means every tangent at the point is Euclidean; the chart is an open neighborhood with the restricted ambient distance; no Holder control of the metric tensor and no bounded-Laplacian coordinates are claimed (Colding-Naber examples show the former can fail). Note the release's family summary says the constant is point dependent, but the manuscript's Theorem 1.1 and abstract say the constant $L_n$ depends only on $n$. No Lean formalization exists for this family.
fields.resultNote: Claims that for every integer $n\ge2$ there is $L_n\ge1$ such that every regular point of every noncollapsed $\mathrm{RCD}(K,n)$ space, $K\in\mathbb R$, has an open neighborhood $L_n$-bi-Lipschitz homeomorphic, with the ambient distance, to an open subset of $\mathbb R^n$; the neighborhood depends on the space and the point. Corollary: an open set of full $\mathcal H^n$ measure containing all regular points carries a countable bi-Lipschitz atlas with $L_n^2$ transition maps. It does NOT claim that the regular set is open, any collapsed or non-RCD statement, or regularity of the metric tensor in the charts.

fields.name: The unassisted classical capacity of the generalized amplitude-damping channel
fields.shortName: Classical capacity of generalized amplitude damping
fields.field: Quantum Shannon theory; channel capacities; Holevo additivity
fields.statement:
The generalized amplitude-damping channel $\mathcal A_{\gamma,
u}$ is the qubit channel modelling energy relaxation with damping $\gamma\in[0,1]$ toward a thermal state with excited population $
u\in[0,1]$. By the Holevo-Schumacher-Westmoreland theorem its unassisted classical capacity is the regularized Holevo information $\lim_n\chi(\mathcal A^{\otimes n})/n$, and since Holevo additivity fails in general (Hastings) the one-use value need not be the answer. Leditzky, Kaur, Datta and Wilde (2018) listed the classical capacity of amplitude damping as open, and Khatri, Sharma and Wilde (2020) gave only upper bounds for the generalized channel; exact values were known only where King's unital theorem or Shor's entanglement-breaking theorem applies. What is the classical capacity of $\mathcal A_{\gamma,
u}$ for all $\gamma,
u$, and does it equal the one-shot Holevo capacity?
fields.posedBy: Leditzky, Kaur, Datta and Wilde, Phys. Rev. A 97 (2018) (amplitude damping open); Khatri, Sharma and Wilde, Phys. Rev. A 102 (2020) (only bounds for the generalized channel)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Leditzky et al. (2018) as naming the classical capacity of ordinary amplitude damping as open; that case was settled by Tang, Zhu, Bai and Wang (2026) for channels with a pure output, which the generalized channel lacks. For the generalized channel the cited sources give bounds (Khatri-Sharma-Wilde, abstract read here) rather than a posing sentence.

The manuscript is credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The capacity theorem has a Lean formalization listed in the release's formalization catalogue.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. The abstract and main theorem were read against the question. formalization.yaml lists ComparatorChallenges/AmplitudeDamping.json with declaration OAI.GAD.main in OAI/InformationTheory/AmplitudeDamping/Main.lean. The comparator statement, read here, says for all $\gamma,\nu\in[0,1]$: the n-use Holevo quantity is n times the one-use value, equals n times an attained one-variable maximum, the operational capacity (defined by codes with collective POVM decoding, not by regularization) equals the one-use Holevo value, and equiprobable phase-pair product ensembles attain it. This is the headline. Additivity with an arbitrary different partner channel, a secondary claim, is not formalized. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote:
Claims that for every $\gamma,
u\in[0,1]$ the unassisted classical capacity of $\mathcal A_{\gamma,
u}$ equals its one-shot Holevo capacity, given by $\max_{p\in[0,1]}[h((1-\gamma)p+\gamma
u)-g(\gamma
u(1-
u)+\gamma(1-\gamma)(p-
u)^2)]$ in bits, with $g$ the entropy of a qubit state of given determinant, attained by two equiprobable pure signals of opposite phase and their independent products. It also claims additivity of one-shot Holevo capacity, minimum output entropy and regularized classical capacity under tensoring with any finite-dimensional channel. It does NOT give the quantum or private capacity of the channel, entanglement-assisted settings, or a closed form for the maximizing $p$.

fields.name: The Hahn-Wilson conjecture: fp-type at most n spectra are exactly the thick subcategory generated by BP<n>
fields.field: Chromatic homotopy theory; stable homotopy theory
fields.statement: Fix a prime $p$. A bounded-below $p$-complete spectrum $X$ is fp if $H^*(X;\mathbb F_p)$ is finitely presented over the Steenrod algebra; it has fp-type at most $n$ if $\pi_*(V\wedge X)$ is finite in total for a finite spectrum $V$ of type $n+1$ (Mahowald-Rezk). Hahn-Wilson redshift shows $K(\mathrm{BP}\langle n\rangle)$ has fp-type $n+1$, and Lee-Pstragowski proved the statement below at height one. The Hahn-Wilson conjecture asks whether finite presentation plus a height bound characterizes finite constructions from truncated Brown-Peterson spectra: is $\{X:\ X\text{ has fp-type at most }n\}=\mathrm{Thick}(\mathrm{BP}\langle n\rangle_p^\wedge)$, the closure under finite sums, shifts, cofiber sequences and retracts, for every $n$ and $p$?
fields.posedBy: Jeremy Hahn and Dylan Wilson (reported from 2021); written as Conjecture 1.1 in David Jongwon Lee and Piotr Pstragowski, The monochromatic Hahn-Wilson conjecture, Inventiones Mathematicae (2026)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript says Lee and Pstragowski give the written formulation (Conjecture 1.1 and Note 1) and report learning it from Dylan Wilson in 2021; yearPosed uses 2021. The first written statement is 2026.

The counterexample is for every sufficiently large prime (no explicit bound read here) and uses one specific regular quotient form of $\mathrm{BP}\langle2\rangle_p^\wedge$; the paper relies on Lee (2026), with Angeltveit-Lind, for independence of the underlying spectrum from the choice of generators at these primes. fields.resultNote: Claims that for every sufficiently large prime $p$ there is a connective $p$-complete spectrum $X$ of exact fp-type two with $X\notin\mathrm{Thick}(\mathrm{BP}\langle2\rangle_p^\wedge)$ for a standard form of $\mathrm{BP}\langle2\rangle$, refuting the universally quantified conjecture at height two. The same $X$ satisfies $L_2^fX\simeq L_2X$ and $L_{T(2)}X\simeq L_{K(2)}X$, so the obstruction lies in how the chromatic pieces are glued, not in a telescope-type failure; the monochromatic form proved by Lee-Pstragowski is untouched. It does NOT treat small primes, heights above two, or the height-one case, which Lee-Pstragowski proved.
